## Problem

`wl delete` and `wl undelete` run an auto-sync after a successful mutation, but that internal sync does not forward the project's `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list to the author-identity gate. The gate therefore runs in *strict* mode and refuses any incoming commit whose author is not the local `user.email` — even when the project explicitly allow-lists that identity for `wl sync`.

Observed 2026-11-22 in the SorraAgents store (`.worklog/config.yaml` allow-lists `sorra@thewizardscode.com`):

```
$ wl delete SA-0MWRDN7TC003VLD0 --reason "..." --json
{"success": true, ...}
Warning: auto-sync after delete failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from
refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 1 incoming commit(s) fail the
author-identity gate.
- db2108e72b: author email 'sorra@thewizardscode.com' does not match configured
  user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'
```

A subsequent explicit `wl sync` in the same checkout merged the same batch without complaint and pushed successfully — proving the allow-list is correct and only the auto-sync path is at fault.

## Root cause

`src/commands/delete.ts` (auto-sync block at ~line 298–311) and `src/commands/undelete.ts` (auto-sync block at ~line 482–495) both do:

```ts
const defaults = getSyncDefaults(config || undefined);
await performSync(dataPath, utils.getDatabase, {
  ...
  gitRemote: defaults.gitRemote,
  gitBranch: defaults.gitBranch,
  // allowForeignAuthor / allowedAuthors never forwarded
});
```

`getSyncDefaults()` returns `allowedAuthors` (and the derived `allowForeignAuthor`), but neither field is passed into `performSync`. The CLI `wl sync` command (`src/commands/sync.ts` ~line 800–840) does forward both, which is why explicit syncs honour the allow-list and auto-syncs do not.

## Consequence

Every `wl delete`/`wl undelete` performed while the remote carries commits from an allow-listed non-local identity prints a scary warning and silently leaves the mutation unpushed. If the operator never runs an explicit `wl sync`, the deletion can be resurrected by a later pull, and agent sessions that assume "delete ⇒ propagated" are misled. It also produces confusing incident noise that looks like an identity misconfiguration.

## Users

- **Operators** using `wl delete`/`wl undelete`: mutations should propagate without a manual follow-up sync, and no spurious identity-gate warning.
- **Agents** running delete/undelete in a worklog-authenticated checkout: their mutation must not be stranded behind a gate that ignores the project's own allow-list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl delete` auto-sync forwards `allowedAuthors` (and `allowForeignAuthor`) from `getSyncDefaults()` into `performSync`, so a commit authored by an allow-listed identity merges without refusal.
- `wl undelete` auto-sync forwards the same fields, with identical semantics.
- Strict mode is preserved: when the config has no allow-list (or `syncAllowedAuthors: []`), a foreign-author commit is still refused by delete/undelete auto-sync, and the existing warning is still printed on refusal.
- The empty-author-email gate is unchanged in all paths (allow-list can never admit an empty author).
- Regression tests cover delete auto-sync and undelete auto-sync: allow-listed author merges; non-allow-listed author refuses with a warning and does not abort the mutation; `--no-sync` still skips the sync entirely.
- Validation: new tests fail on the current code (gate refuses the allow-listed author) and pass after the fix.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Deleting or restoring a work item in a project that allow-lists a second (operator or agent) identity now propagates on its own instead of printing a false identity-gate failure and stranding the change until someone runs `wl sync` manually.

## Constraints

- Do not widen the gate: the fix forwards *the project's configured allow-list*, never an allow-all. `syncAllowedAuthors: []` must remain strict.
- Do not change `performSync`'s option contract in a way that breaks the CLI path (`src/commands/sync.ts`).
- Keep the "sync failure must not abort the delete/restore" contract: a genuine refusal still warns and leaves the local mutation intact.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — forward `allowedAuthors` / `allowForeignAuthor` from `getSyncDefaults()` into the auto-sync `performSync` call
- `src/commands/undelete.ts` — same fix for the restore auto-sync
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `getSyncDefaults()` and the `performSync` options contract (read-only; must not break)
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync-allow-list.test.ts` — new delete regression suite (allow-listed vs strict author)
- `tests/cli/undelete-auto-sync-allow-list.test.ts` — new undelete regression suite (allow-listed vs strict author)
- `docs/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` — note that delete/undelete auto-sync honours the same allow-list

## Related work

- WL-0MTGDW58X007UJDS — Replace binary author-identity gate with configurable author whitelist (origin of `syncAllowedAuthors`)
- WL-0MVMZP6A5005PB66 — wl sync blocked: identity gate refuses 7 commits authored by sorra@thewizardscode.com (the incident that allow-listed this identity for explicit syncs)
- WL-0MWGO5L41006PPPS / WL-0MWGO5JUJ008EK4M — push-side identity guard (separate, still open)
- discovered-from: SA-0MWRDN7TC003VLD0 (SorraAgents; `wl delete` auto-sync refused an allow-listed author on 2026-11-22)

## Risks & Assumptions

- Risk: forwarding `allowForeignAuthor` could be read as "allow all". Mitigation: `getSyncDefaults()` only derives `allowForeignAuthor: true` from the legacy `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` key; an explicit `syncAllowedAuthors` list keeps it false, so only listed emails pass.
- Assumption: `getSyncDefaults()` is the single source of truth for both fields (confirmed: `src/commands/sync.ts` lines ~31–52).
- Scope-creep risk: any other internal `performSync` caller may have the same omission — audit them all as part of this item rather than in follow-ups.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTGDW58X007UJDS** – Replace binary author-identity gate with configurable author whitelist (completed)
- **WL-0MTGH78A4000ZVNB** – Author-identity gate refusal must surface at default verbosity and exit non-zero (completed)
- **WL-0MVMZP6A5005PB66** – wl sync blocked: identity gate refuses 7 commits authored by sorra@thewizardscode.com (completed)

### Repository file matches

data.description:
## Problem

`run_tests.py` caches suite verdicts keyed on a git-state fingerprint (HEAD SHA + a content hash of every path `git status --porcelain` reports as dirty). Build output (`packages/shared/dist/`, `packages/*/dist/`, etc.) is **gitignored**, so rebuilding that artefact does not change the git state. A cached failure whose cause was stale/missing build output therefore keeps being replayed for the whole failure TTL (5 minutes) — and re-recorded post-run — instead of re-executing.

Observed while implementing WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE (the shared-build freshness preflight):

1. Fresh worktree with no `packages/shared/dist`: the preflight aborts the run (`Refusing to run the suite…`); the failure is cached.
2. `npm run build:shared` in the same worktree: the build is now fresh.
3. Re-run `run_tests.py --scope changed` **without** `--force`: the identical failure is replayed from cache (`node: FAIL`), so the documented remedy appears not to work.
4. `run_tests.py --force`: PASS; the refreshed entry then serves subsequent runs.

The same shape applies to any failure whose cause is invisible to the git fingerprint (a stale root `dist/`, a stale shared build, a wiped build tree).

## Users

- **Agent running a full-suite or changed-scope run from a long-lived checkout**: when a cached failure came from stale build output, the agent wastes time debugging correct code, then has to discover `--force` to make progress.
- **Audit tier reading cache evidence**: a cached red caused by a build precondition produces a false "code defect" signal in the audit pipeline.

### User stories

- As an implementing agent, I want `run_tests.py` to re-execute when the workspace build has been refreshed since a cached failure was recorded, so a rebuild is enough and I do not need to remember `--force`.
- As a producer reading an audit report, I want cached failures to reflect the current workspace state, so a red suite means the code is actually broken.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A cached **pass** is still served exactly as today (no regression to the audit cache contract).
2. A cached **failure** is not replayed when the workspace build output has been written since the entry was recorded; the command re-executes instead.
3. Regression test with a controlled-mtime fixture: a failing run, then a build-style artefact write, then the second run executes rather than replaying (red-first: the same test asserts a cache hit before the artefact write).
4. `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (and any cache documentation) updated; the temporary `--force` workaround note added by WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE in the shared-build section is removed once this lands.
5. Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Impact

Agents running test suites no longer chase phantom failures caused by a cached verdict replayed after a rebuild, so a red suite once again reflects the current code state.

## Constraints

- **No regression to the pass contract**: cached green verdicts must continue to serve exactly as today.
- **Scope limited to failure invalidation**: the change only affects when a cached failure is served; pass caching is untouched.
- **Bounded artefact set**: compare only known build artefacts that are test preconditions (the resolved `packages/shared/dist` and the root `dist/`), not every gitignored path — enumerating arbitrary gitignored files is unbounded and slow.
- **Cheap on lookup**: the freshness check must not add a full-tree filesystem walk to every cache hit; reuse the resolution logic the shared-build preflight already uses.
- **mtime is a heuristic**: a branch switch or `git checkout` can make sources newer than build output without a content change (a false rebuild recommendation), and a restored/copied `dist` can carry an older mtime with newer content. Document the trade-off; do not attempt content hashing here.
- **Global skill code**: the runner and cache live in the agent framework repo (see *Repo note*). This item is the recorded home for the runner-side fix.

## Repo note (cross-repo change)

The work item is stored in the **ContextHub** worklog (`WL-` prefix), but the code to change is the **agent framework's** test skill:

- `skill/test_cache.py` and `skill/test/run_tests.py` live in the framework repo (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/`, exposed as the global skills install via the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink), **not** in ContextHub's tree.
- The cache documentation (`docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md`) lives in **ContextHub**.

Precedent: recent `WL-` items were committed into the SorraAgents repo while tracked in the ContextHub worklog, so a cross-repo change is the established shape. Plan/implement must confirm which checkout/worktree the code change lands in before starting.

## Existing state

- `skill/test_cache.py` — git-state fingerprint (`compute_git_state`: HEAD SHA + content hash of dirty paths); 2-hour TTL for green, 5-minute TTL for failed runs (`FAILED_RUN_TTL_SECONDS`); entries record `git_state`, `git_state_at_start`, `exit_code`, `completed_at`, `fingerprint_kind` (`worktree`/`tree`/`change_set`).
- `skill/test/run_tests.py` — orchestrates the run, invokes the cache, and applies the shared-build freshness preflight added by WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE (aborts on stale/missing build output).
- The preflight abort is a non-zero exit, so it is cached as a failed verdict, then replayed on the next run — the core of the bug.
- Build output is gitignored by design, so `npm run build` never changes the cache key.

## Desired design direction

**Recommended: refuse a cached failure when build output changed.** On cache lookup for an entry with `exit_code != 0`, compare the entry's recorded `completed_at` against the mtime of the resolved build artefacts; if any artefact is newer than the entry, treat it as a miss and re-execute. On a pass (`exit_code == 0`) the existing lookup is unchanged.

Why this direction:

- Most general — covers any gitignored artefact that is a test precondition, not just one failure reason.
- Smallest change to the cache module and preserves the pass contract by construction.
- Directly fixes the observed preflight-abort-then-rebuild case: the rebuild writes newer artefacts, so the next lookup misses.

Alternatives considered:

1. **Exclude build-precondition failures from being stored** — requires classifying failure reasons at write time (fragile: the same abort can arise from several causes).
2. **Extend the fingerprint with build-artefact hashes** — changes every cache key, discarding valid pass hits for unchanged builds and paying hashing cost on every run.

## Key Files

- `skill/test_cache.py` — `run_cached()` / `query_cached()` lookup path, plus a small helper that returns the newest mtime of the resolved build artefacts; the failed-entry freshness gate lives here. **Primary change location.**
- `skill/test/run_tests.py` — where the shared-build preflight already resolves the artefacts; reuse that resolution (or export it) rather than duplicating path logic.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` — regression coverage with controlled-mtime fixtures (red-first: assert a cache hit, then write a newer build artefact, then assert a miss/execute).
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (ContextHub) — cache-evidence documentation; note the failure-invalidation rule and remove the `--force` workaround once this lands.

## Related work

- **WL-0MW8G1X3V007CGAE** — Full-suite runs in an existing checkout silently use a stale `@worklog/shared` build (in-progress, plan_complete). Adds the build-stale **preflight**; this item makes the **cache** honour a rebuild. Together: preflight catches stale builds on fresh runs, cache invalidation stops replaying the stale red.
- **WL-0MVPO9P610055UQ3** — Test-run cache returns stale results when only the contents of already-modified files change (completed). Direct precedent for cache-freshness correctness.
- **WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O** — Redirect post-push verification full-suite runs to a pinned isolated worktree (completed). Related cache-evidence work.
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` — the cache-evidence contract this item's docs update touches.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — false positives on mtime.** A `git checkout` can make sources newer than build output without content changes, causing an unnecessary re-execution. Mitigation: the cost is one suite run, not lost debugging time; document the trade-off.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Expanding the artefact set beyond the known build preconditions. Mitigation: scope to the shared build and root `dist/`; generalise only on evidence of other artefacts causing the same pattern.
- **Risk — filesystem mtime precision.** Coarse-granularity filesystems (FAT, some network mounts) can mask a rebuild within the same second. Mitigation: accept; it is an edge case and the 5-minute failed TTL already limits exposure.
- **Assumption —** the runner can resolve the same artefacts the preflight resolves (shared build via `node_modules/@worklog/shared`, root `dist/` via repo layout).
- **Assumption —** entries already store `completed_at` and `exit_code`, so the freshness check needs no schema change (a migration-free change).
- **Assumption —** a cross-repo change (code in the framework repo, docs in ContextHub) is acceptable and matches recent `WL-` precedent.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the fix invalidate cached failures for any gitignored artefact change, or only build output?" — Answer: only build output that is a test precondition. Scoped to the known build artefact directories (shared build, root `dist/`), not arbitrary ignored paths. Source: item description + constraint reasoning.
- Q: "Does the preflight failure itself get cached?" — Answer: yes. The preflight abort is a non-zero exit cached as a failed verdict. This is the concrete mechanism of the bug; the recommended direction invalidates it because the rebuild writes newer artefacts than the entry's `completed_at`. Source: `test_cache.py` docstring (`FAILED_RUN_TTL_SECONDS`) + the observed reproduction in the item description.
- Q: "Which repository owns the code change?" — Answer: the agent framework repo (SorraAgents), which holds `skill/test_cache.py` and `skill/test/run_tests.py`; the ContextHub worklog is the recorded home and holds `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md`. Evidence: `find`/`grep` of both checkouts, the `~/.pi/agent/skills → SorraAgents/skill` symlink, and recent `WL-` commits in the SorraAgents log.

- **WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6** – Remove unused WorkItem import from index.ts (completed)

## Description

`wl delete` runs an auto-sync after a successful mutation, but the internal `performSync` call does **not** forward the project's `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list (nor the derived `allowForeignAuthor`) from `getSyncDefaults()`. The author-identity gate therefore runs in strict mode and refuses any incoming commit whose author is not the local `user.email` — even when the project explicitly allow-lists that identity for `wl sync`.

**Root cause:** `src/commands/delete.ts` (~line 298) builds the `performSync` options from `getSyncDefaults()` but only passes `gitRemote` and `gitBranch`, dropping `allowedAuthors` and `allowForeignAuthor`. The CLI `wl sync` command (`src/commands/sync.ts` ~line 800-834) correctly forwards both, which is why explicit syncs honour the allow-list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl delete` auto-sync forwards `allowedAuthors` (and `allowForeignAuthor`) from `getSyncDefaults()` into `performSync`, so a commit authored by an allow-listed identity merges without refusal.
- Strict mode is preserved: when the config has no allow-list (or `syncAllowedAuthors: []`), a foreign-author commit is still refused by delete auto-sync, and the existing warning is still printed on refusal.
- The empty-author-email gate is unchanged: an allow-list can never admit an empty author.
- The "sync failure must not abort the delete" contract is preserved: a genuine refusal still warns and leaves the local mutation intact.
- `--no-sync` still skips the auto-sync entirely.
- The delete regression tests (`tests/cli/delete-auto-sync-allow-list.test.ts`) pass.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` option contract is unchanged (no breaking change to the CLI sync path).

## Implementation Notes

In `src/commands/delete.ts`, in the auto-sync block:

```ts
const defaults = getSyncDefaults(config || undefined);
await performSync(dataPath, utils.getDatabase, {
  file: dataPath,
  prefix: options.prefix,
  gitRemote: defaults.gitRemote,
  gitBranch: defaults.gitBranch,
  allowedAuthors: defaults.allowedAuthors,        // <-- add
  allowForeignAuthor: defaults.allowForeignAuthor, // <-- add
  push: true,
  dryRun: false,
  silent: true,
  isJsonMode,
  isVerbose: false,
});
```

`performSync` already accepts both fields in its options interface (`src/commands/sync.ts` lines 76-77).

## Deliverables

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — forward `allowedAuthors` / `allowForeignAuthor` from `getSyncDefaults()` into the auto-sync `performSync` call
- Code comment documenting why the allow-list is forwarded (parity with `wl sync`)

**Key Files:**

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — the fix (auto-sync `performSync` call, ~line 298)
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `getSyncDefaults()` and `performSync` options interface
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync-allow-list.test.ts` — regression tests (from test feature)

## Description

Update documentation to reflect that `wl delete` and `wl undelete` auto-sync honours the project's `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list, exactly as `wl sync` does.

The bug (WL-0MWRQYK3X007RQ1T) caused a false identity-gate refusal on every delete/restore in a store where the remote carries commits from an allow-listed non-local identity. The fix makes the auto-sync forward the allow-list; the docs must state this parity so operators do not mistake a future refusal for a misconfiguration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- `docs/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` documents that `wl delete` and `wl undelete` auto-sync honours `syncAllowedAuthors` and `allowForeignAuthor`, with the same strict-mode and empty-author-email semantics as `wl sync`.
- `./DATA_SYNCING.md` (the sync configuration reference that documents `syncAllowedAuthors` and the author-identity gate) notes that delete/undelete auto-sync runs the same gate with the same allow-list.
- `docs/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` notes the failure mode this fixes: an auto-sync refusal that does NOT abort the mutation and leaves the change unpushed until a manual `wl sync`.
- Code comments in `src/commands/delete.ts` and `src/commands/undelete.ts` explain why the allow-list is forwarded (parity with `wl sync`) and why the gate is not widened (`getSyncDefaults()` only derives `allowForeignAuthor: true` from the legacy `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` key; `syncAllowedAuthors: []` stays strict).
- Any related docs (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `./CLI.md`, `./README.md`, `docs/tutorials/02-team-collaboration.md`) that describe delete/undelete sync behaviour are cross-checked; update only where the allow-list parity is materially relevant.
- Documentation changes are accurate for both the allow-listed and strict configurations.

## Goal

Make the producer-review provenance audit a packaged, repeatable read-only command so a re-run cannot drift from the dispatcher predicates the way the manual 2026-11-23 audit did (discovered-from:WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV).

## Problem statement

The provenance rule exists as pure, tested code (`classifyProducerReviewProvenance` / `assembleProducerReviewProvenance`), but nothing packages it into a runnable command: every audit is a one-off script that re-collects comments, audit records, dispatch markers and dependency edges by hand. The recorded 2026-11-23 audit (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI) demonstrates the failure mode — for `AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P` it supplied `dependency` as an independent hold from six **inbound `depended-on-by`** edges instead of outbound `depends-on` edges, so the live re-run regraded the row `needs-producer-input`. A wrongful clear was avoided only because the clearing follow-up happened to re-check the live set first.

## Users

- **Dispatcher maintainer / operator** — needs to answer "which prep items are producer-review flagged, why, how old is that evidence, and which can be cleared now?" for any root at any (including past) instant, without writing code.
- **Remediation agent** (downtime worker or `implement` session) — needs a diff-stable machine payload it can quote as the seed evidence set for a clearing run.

User stories:

- As a dispatcher maintainer, I want one command that reports every prep-stage `needsProducerReview=true` row per root with its flag source, deciding evidence, age, open question and holds, so that a stale flag is distinguishable from a live producer question.
- As a remediation agent, I want a deterministic `--now` replay whose holds come from the dispatcher's own predicates, so that the `can-clear-now` set I clear is provably safe to clear.
- As a reviewer, I want byte-identical output for the same `--now`, so that two audits of the same window can be diffed in review.

## Context

The provenance rule lives in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` (pure functions: plain data in, verdict out — no `wl` call, no subprocess, no file write) and is documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Producer-review provenance*, with the recorded audit in *Recorded producer-review provenance audit (2026-11-23 22:15Z)* and the clearing run in *Stale-flag clearing run*.

The prep-supply read already has an equivalent packaged command — `packages/herdr/src/prep-supply-report-cli.ts`, published as the `worklog-prep-supply` bin — which owns argument parsing, root resolution, output and an injected read-only I/O seam, plus a documented section (*Prep-supply report command*). Provenance has no equivalent, so every audit re-implements the read side, which is exactly where the edge direction was got wrong. This item mirrors the prep-supply command's shape for provenance rather than inventing a new one.

## Existing state

- `downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` (521 lines) exports `PRODUCER_REVIEW_SOURCES`, `PRODUCER_REVIEW_GROUPS`, `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput` / `Verdict` / `Table`, `classifyProducerReviewProvenance`, `assembleProducerReviewProvenance` and `formatProducerReviewAge`. `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput.holds` already accepts the gate tokens (`dependency`, `assignee-hold`, `startOn`, `attempt-budget`, `cooldown`, `dispatch-marker`) but nothing populates them from live reads.
- Holding/predicate logic already exists and must be **reused, not restated**: `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`) for `assignee-hold` / `startOnNotReached` / `not-dispatchable`, `parseDepListBlockersOutput` (`downtime-worker.parsers.ts`) which keeps only outbound `direction === 'depends-on'` edges, and `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` / `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` for the worker-side gates.
- The read side already exists as an injected seam: `createPrepSupplyReportDeps()` (`downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts`) wires the consolidated `wl worklist --json` read, the per-root `wl list --json` fallback per prep stage, batched dependency edges (in-process with a per-item `wl dep list --json` fallback) and the rolling dispatch log (`<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`).
- That seam has **no comment or stored-audit read** — the classifier's two remaining evidence sources have no helper: comments come from `wl show <id> --json` and the stored audit record from `wl audit-show <id> --json`. Only `auditResult` (the item-level mirror on `wl show`) is currently reachable, and the rule requires the stored record's `readyToClose`/`generatedAt`.
- No provenance audit command, bin entry or docs section exists.

## Desired change

A new read-only command (source + built bin, following the prep-supply pattern) that, for every prep-stage item carrying `needsProducerReview=true` on each requested root, emits one provenance row: `id`, `root`, `source`, deciding evidence reference, flag age, open question, holds, group — as a human table plus a per-root JSON payload. Holds are computed from the dispatcher/gate predicates over **outbound** `depends-on` edges only. `--root` (repeatable) and `--now` (ISO-8601) allow an exact replay; output is sorted and byte-stable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A read-only command/diagnostic emits per-root JSON plus a human table of provenance rows (`id`, source, deciding evidence reference, flag age, open question, holds, group) for every prep-stage `needsProducerReview=true` item.
2. Holds are derived from the dispatcher/gate predicates (outbound non-terminal `depends-on` edges, `assignee`, `startOn`, attempt budget, cooldown, dispatch marker), never from inbound edges; a regression test pins that an inbound `depended-on-by` edge is not a hold.
3. `--root` (repeatable) and `--now` are supported for a deterministic replay; output is stable and diffable.
4. Strictly read-only: no flag, assignee or marker mutation (regression test).
5. Usage and the `--now`/hold semantics are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`; changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only, proven not asserted.** No `wl update`, no `wl reviewed`, no marker write, no `getDefaultSettingsPath()` (it `mkdir`s the config dir); registry path resolution follows the prep-supply command's pure-read approach.
- **One source of truth for holds.** Reuse `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` and `isNonTerminalCooldownActive`; do not fork a second copy of any predicate.
- **Fail closed.** An unreadable root or unparseable payload is reported as an error (named on stderr, exit `1`), never rendered as an empty healthy row set — mirroring the prep-supply exit-code contract (`0` success, `1` partial root failure, `2` usage/no roots).
- **Stable ordering.** Roots sorted by path, rows by item id; `flagAgeMs: null` renders as `unknown` via `formatProducerReviewAge`, never as a fabricated age.
- **UK English** in code comments, docs and output copy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Wrong-direction edges (the discovered-from bug).** Mitigation: AC2's regression test plus reuse of `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, which already filters to `direction === 'depends-on'`.
- **Predicate drift.** The audit could pass its own tests while diverging from the live dispatcher. Mitigation: the command quotes predicate outputs rather than paraphrasing, and the docs section states the audit reads the dispatcher's predicates.
- **Accidental write.** Risk that a "helpful" code path clears or reassigns. Mitigation: AC4 regression test asserting item/flag state and the dispatch marker log are byte-identical before and after a run.
- **Scope creep.** Clearing flags (WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV), batching producer interviews, reassigning items and any dispatch/gate/skill behaviour change are **out of scope** and belong to their own items.
- **Read cost.** Comments and the stored audit record are per-item reads (`wl show`, `wl audit-show`), not part of the batched worklist pass. The bound is the flagged prep set (18 rows across four roots in the 2026-11-23 audit), so per-item reads are acceptable; the command must not fan out to every prep item.
- **Assumption:** prep-stage supply is `idea` + `intake_complete` (`PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES`), matching the recorded audit's population; the command reuses that constant rather than redefining the stage set.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.ts` — new pure collection/assembly layer: per-root rows for flagged prep items, populating `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput.holds` from the gate predicates.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.ts` — new CLI entry: argument parsing (`--root` repeatable, `--now`, `--json`, `--help`), root resolution, exit codes, output.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.test.ts` + `...provenance-audit-cli.test.ts` — AC1–AC4 regressions (row shape, inbound-edge-is-not-a-hold, `--now` replay stability, read-only).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` — existing classifier, reused unchanged (its `holds` input is the seam this item fills).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts` — reuse `createPrepSupplyReportDeps()` as the read-only I/O seam; extend it (or add a sibling source module) with the two missing reads: `wl show <id> --json` for comments and `wl audit-show <id> --json` for the stored audit record.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parsers.ts` — `parseDepListBlockersOutput` (outbound `depends-on` only).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — new `bin` entry (`worklog-provenance-audit` → `dist/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.js`).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — new `### Provenance audit command (WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P, child of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD)` section after *Producer-review provenance*, modelled on *Prep-supply report command*.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWTBJ7G1004Y29B — Prep-supply report command** (completed). The direct template: same argument/root/`--now`/exit-code/read-only contract. This item mirrors its shape for provenance; it deliberately does *not* duplicate its buckets.
- **WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI — Producer-review provenance audit** (completed). Recorded the audit by hand and produced the rule; this item packages the run that recorded it.
- **WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV — Clear stale needsProducerReview flags proven clearable by the provenance audit** (in-progress). The consumer: its AC1 asks for a "documented `--now` read" — this command is that read.
- **WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD — Prep backlog is almost entirely producer-review flagged** (open; the epic that both the recorded audit and the clearing run are children of). Scope item 4a's audit needs a repeatable runner.
- **WL-0MWTVPL1A005KB4D — Change intake/plan/interview skills so routine questions do not park items behind producer review** (open). Reduces future flag volume; independent of this command.
- **WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER — Batch producer interviews for prep items grouped needs-producer-input** (open). The sibling follow-up (4b): consumes the `needs-producer-input` group this command emits.
- **WL-0MVI0IS6Y0028KTO — Read cache: worklist invocation as one cache entry** (completed). Relevant if the command's per-item `wl show` / `wl audit-show` reads ever need caching; not required here (the flagged set is small).
- Docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Producer-review provenance*, *Recorded producer-review provenance audit*, *Stale-flag clearing run*, *Prep-supply report command*.

## Related work (automated report)

`/skill:find-related WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P` found 3 related items and 3 repository file matches:

- **WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI** – Producer-review provenance audit (completed)
- **WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER** – Batch producer interviews for prep items grouped needs-producer-input (open)
- **WL-0MVI0IS6Y0028KTO** – Read cache: worklist invocation as one cache entry (completed)
- Repository matches: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `CLI.md`.

## Duplicate check

Searched `wl search "provenance audit holds"` and `wl search "prep-supply-report-cli"`, and reviewed `WL-0MWTBJ7G1004Y29B` (prep-supply report command — a different report: supply buckets, not provenance rows), `WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI` (the completed manual audit), `WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV` (the clearing run) and `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD` (the parent). None packages a repeatable provenance command. No duplicate; no acceptance criterion of this item is already satisfied.

## Out of scope

Clearing flags, reassigning items, or any dispatch/gate/skill behaviour change.

## Impact

An operator can re-run the provenance audit as one command whose holds come from the same predicates the dispatcher uses, instead of hand-collecting edges that can be read in the wrong direction.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were needed: the seed description carried the goal, the failure that motivates it (the inbound-vs-outbound edge direction in `AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P`), the five acceptance criteria, the out-of-scope boundary and the impact. The remaining detail was resolved by repository research rather than by asking the producer:

- Q: "Which module owns the provenance rule, and is it already pure?" — Answer (repo research, no question asked): `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts`; exports `classifyProducerReviewProvenance` / `assembleProducerReviewProvenance` / `formatProducerReviewAge` and takes `holds` as an input field that nothing yet populates. Source: `grep -n "^export " packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts`.
- Q: "Is there an existing read-only command to copy?" — Answer (repo research): yes, `packages/herdr/src/prep-supply-report-cli.ts` + `createPrepSupplyReportDeps()`; documented in *Prep-supply report command*. Source: `packages/herdr/package.json` `bin` (`worklog-prep-supply`).
- Q: "Where do holds come from today?" — Answer (repo research): `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`assignee-hold`, `startOnNotReached`), `parseDepListBlockersOutput` (outbound `depends-on` only), `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`, `isNonTerminalCooldownActive`; the inbound `depended-on-by` direction is never a blocker. Source: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parsers.ts:381-415`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts:890-1005`.
- Q: "Which stages count as prep supply?" — Answer (repo research): `PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES = ['idea', 'intake_complete']`, matching the recorded audit's population. Source: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts:76-81`.

## Goal

Provide the **read side** of the repeatable producer-review provenance audit: one injectable, strictly read-only seam that turns a worklog root into everything `classifyProducerReviewProvenance` needs for that root's flagged prep set.

Child 1 of 4 of WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P (child of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD). It is the acquisition half only; classification/assembly is child 2 and the command surface is child 3.

## User story

As a remediation agent, I want comments, the stored audit record and dependency edges for the flagged prep set read through one injectable seam, so that the audit cannot re-implement the read side (which is where the edge direction was got wrong in the 2026-11-23 audit).

## Context

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts` already owns the read pattern to copy: `createPrepSupplyReportDeps()` wires `wl worklist --json`, a per-root `wl list --json` fallback per prep stage, batched in-process dependency edges with a per-item `wl dep list --json` fallback, and the rolling dispatch log. Its header documents the read-only contract.
- That seam has **no comment and no stored-audit read**. Confirmed payload shapes:
  - `wl show <id> --json` returns `{ success, workItem, comments, auditResult, auditWaiver }` — `comments[]` carry `{ id, workItemId, author, comment, createdAt, references }`.
  - `wl audit-show <id> --json` returns `{ success, workItemId, audit: null }` or `{ success, workItemId, audit: { readyToClose, auditedAt, summary, rawOutput, author, fingerprint } }`.
- `parseDepListBlockersOutput` (`downtime-worker.parsers.ts`) keeps only `direction === 'depends-on'` (outbound) edges — the exact predicate that prevents the inbound `depended-on-by` misread.
- `PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES` (`downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts`) is `['idea', 'intake_complete']` and must be reused, not redefined.
- Per-item reads are acceptable because the bound is the flagged prep set (18 rows across four roots in the 2026-11-23 audit); the seam must not fan out to every prep item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new read-only source module, sibling to `downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts`, exposes an injectable seam that returns per root: the flagged prep set, per-item comments, per-item stored audit record, outbound dependency blocker refs and the rolling dispatch-log entries.
- The flagged set is read with `wl list --json --needs-producer-review --include-not-started` and filtered to `PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES` (the constant is imported, never redefined).
- Comments are mapped from `wl show <id> --json` `comments[]` onto `ProducerReviewComment` and the stored record from `wl audit-show <id> --json` `audit` onto `ProducerReviewAuditRecord` (`audit: null` maps to "no stored record", not an error).
- Dependency edges are read through the existing batched in-process reader with the per-item `wl dep list --json` fallback and filtered by `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, so only outbound `depends-on` edges survive.
- A malformed or unparseable payload for a root is surfaced as that root's error (fail-closed) and named; it is never rendered as an empty, healthy set, while other roots still read.
- Strictly read-only: no flag, assignee or marker mutation (regression test). Write surfaces are injected to throw if called, and the dispatch-log file bytes are asserted unchanged after a run.
- Tests are written first and cover: flagged-set parsing, `wl show` comment parsing, `audit-show` null and record parsing, outbound-only edge filtering, and fail-closed on malformed JSON.

## Minimal implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-source.ts` — new module: `createProvenanceAuditDeps()` plus pure parsers (`parseFlaggedPrepItems`, `parseShowComments`, `parseAuditRecord`, `parseDepListBlockersOutput` reuse).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-source.test.ts` — the AC regressions (test-first).
- Reuse, unchanged: `spawnCliStdout` / `buildWlArgsForRoot` / `getExecFileAsync` (`cli-spawn.ts`, `fetcher.args.ts`), `readOutboundDepsInProcess` / `withInProcessDb` (`fetcher.inprocess.ts`), `readDowntimeLogEntries` (`downtime-log-entries.ts`), `parseDepListBlockersOutput` (`downtime-worker.parsers.ts`), `PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES` (`downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts`), and the `ProducerReviewComment` / `ProducerReviewAuditRecord` types from `downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts`.
- No new dependency; no changes to the prep-supply module's contract.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-source.ts` — new read seam + parsers.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-source.test.ts` — AC1/AC2/AC6 regressions.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply-source.ts` — the pattern to mirror (unchanged).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` — the target types (unchanged).

## Constraints

- Read-only, proven not asserted: no `wl update`, no `wl reviewed`, no marker write, no `getDefaultSettingsPath()`; per-root scope via the per-call `--worklog-dir` argument vector, never a module-global override.
- Fail closed on unreadable roots and unparseable payloads.
- UK English in code comments and docs.
- No caching layer (WL-0MVI0IS6Y0028KTO is not required here; the flagged set is small).

## Out of scope

Holds derivation (child 2), the CLI/command surface (child 3), docs (child 4), and any flag clearing, reassignment or dispatch/gate behaviour change.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the fixtures and harness (child 1).

## Goal

Provide the **pure assembly half** of the repeatable producer-review provenance audit: turn the read seam's per-item data into provenance rows whose `holds` are computed from the dispatcher's own gate predicates over **outbound** `depends-on` edges only.

Child 2 of 4 of WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P (child of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD). It fills the one seam the existing rule left open: `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput.holds` is already accepted but nothing populates it.

## User story

As a remediation agent, I want the `can-clear-now` set to come from the dispatcher's own predicates, so that the flags I clear are provably safe to clear and the inbound-`depended-on-by` misread of the 2026-11-23 audit cannot recur.

## Context

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` already implements the rule as pure functions: `classifyProducerReviewProvenance(input)` (plain data in, verdict out) and `assembleProducerReviewProvenance(rows)` (id-sorted rows + groups). It must be **reused unchanged**; this child only fills `holds` and adds `root`.
- The hold vocabulary is `dependency`, `assignee-hold`, `startOn`, `attempt-budget`, `cooldown`, `dispatch-marker`.
- Predicates to reuse, never restate: `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`, gates `assignee-hold` / `startOnNotReached` / `not-dispatchable`), `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`), `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` and `dispatchedItemMarkers` / `markerStillExcludes` (`downtime-log-markers.ts`), `prepSupplyKindForStage` (`downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts`), and the outbound-only edge predicate (`TERMINAL_STATUSES` semantics: an unresolvable or non-terminal blocker is unmet).
- **Critical subtlety:** `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` returns `producer-review` first when `needsProducerReview === true`, and every audited item carries that flag. The holds derivation must therefore call it with `needsProducerReview` masked to `false` (never mutating the item), or the assignee/`startOn` holds would never be observed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new pure module `downtime-worker.provenance-audit.ts` emits, per root, one row per prep-stage `needsProducerReview=true` item, each row carrying `id`, `root`, `source`, the deciding evidence reference, the flag age, the open-question marker, the holds and the group (AC1).
- Rows are produced by calling `classifyProducerReviewProvenance` unchanged and grouping them with `assembleProducerReviewProvenance`; the flag age renders as `unknown` when `flagAgeMs` is `null` via the existing `formatProducerReviewAge`.
- `holds` are derived by reusing the dispatcher predicates: `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` with `needsProducerReview` masked for `assignee-hold` and `startOn`; outbound non-terminal `depends-on` edges for `dependency`; `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` for `attempt-budget`; `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` for `cooldown`; the stage-guard marker predicate for `dispatch-marker`.
- A regression test pins that an inbound `depended-on-by` edge is never a hold, that an outbound non-terminal `depends-on` edge is a `dependency` hold, and that an outbound edge whose blocker is `completed`/`deleted` is not a hold (AC2).
- Output is deterministic: rows sorted by item id and roots sorted by path, so the same inputs in a different order produce identical output.
- The module performs no I/O (no `node:fs`, no `node:child_process`, no spawn seam), making read-only-ness structural rather than asserted; tests are written first.

## Minimal implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.ts` — new pure module: `buildProvenanceAuditReport(inputs, options)` (pure), `deriveProvenanceHolds(item, ctx)` (the gate-predicate reuse), row types adding `root`, and a stable assembly/render helper set.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.test.ts` — AC1–AC5 regressions (test-first), including the inbound-edge pin.
- Reuse: `classifyProducerReviewProvenance`, `assembleProducerReviewProvenance`, `formatProducerReviewAge`, `PRODUCER_REVIEW_SOURCES`, `PRODUCER_REVIEW_GROUPS` (`downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts`); `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`); `isNonTerminalCooldownActive`, `dispatchedItemMarkers`, `markerStillExcludes` (`downtime-log-markers.ts`); `prepSupplyKindForStage`, `PREP_SUPPLY_STAGES` (`downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts`); `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_NON_TERMINAL_COOLDOWN_MS`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` (`downtime-worker.constants.ts`).
- Holds are additive, not exclusive: a row reports every hold that applies, because the audit answers "what holds this item" rather than "what is the primary bucket" (the prep-supply classifier's precedence is deliberately not copied).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.ts` — new pure assembly + hold derivation.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.test.ts` — AC regressions, including the inbound-edge pin.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` — reused unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-markers.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts` — reused predicates (unchanged).

## Constraints

- One source of truth for holds: no second copy of any predicate; if a predicate is missing, export it from its owning module rather than duplicating it.
- `null` age renders `unknown`, never a fabricated age.
- No mutation of the input data (the suite freezes inputs to prove it).
- UK English in code comments.

## Out of scope

Reading (child 1), the CLI surface (child 3), docs (child 4), and any dispatch/gate behaviour change.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the fixtures (child 1) and the read seam (child 2) for its input types.

## Goal

Package the provenance audit as the operator-facing **read-only command**: `worklog-provenance-audit`, with a repeatable `--root`, a frozen `--now`, a human table plus a per-root JSON payload, the prep-supply exit-code contract, and a proven read-only guarantee.

Child 3 of 4 of WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P (child of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD). It is the end-to-end slice the operator runs; child 4 documents it.

## User story

As a dispatcher maintainer, I want one command that reports every prep-stage `needsProducerReview=true` row per root with its flag source, deciding evidence, age, open question and holds, so that two audits of the same window diff byte-for-byte in review.

## Context

- `packages/herdr/src/prep-supply-report-cli.ts` is the template: argument parsing, root resolution, output, injected I/O seam, `--now` replay and the `0/1/2` exit-code contract, published as `worklog-prep-supply`. This child mirrors that shape rather than inventing a new one.
- The pure assembly (child 2) and its read seam (child 1) already exist; this child owns only parsing, root resolution, wiring and output.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` `bin` currently maps `worklog-pane-close` and `worklog-prep-supply`; `build:only` chmods the built entries.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new CLI module `downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.ts` follows the prep-supply CLI shape: `--root` (repeatable, deduped), `--now <iso>`, `--json`, `-h/--help`, and root resolution from the `downtimeWorklogRoots` registry when `--root` is omitted, using a pure-read settings path (never `getDefaultSettingsPath()`, which `mkdir`s the config directory).
- Default output is the human table followed by the per-root JSON payload; `--json` emits the payload alone; the table carries one row per flagged item with `id`, `source`, deciding evidence reference, flag age, open question, holds and group (AC1).
- `--root` (repeatable) and `--now` are supported for a deterministic replay; output is stable and diffable (AC3) — roots sorted by path, rows by item id, two runs at the same `--now` byte-identical, a later `--now` changing only the ages.
- Exit codes mirror prep-supply: `0` success; `1` one or more roots failed to read (the other roots are still reported and the failure is named on stderr); `2` usage error or no roots available.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` gains the `worklog-provenance-audit` bin mapping to `dist/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.js`, and `build:only` chmods it.
- Strictly read-only: no flag, assignee or marker mutation (regression test).
- Tests are written first and consume the fixtures and harness from child 1, covering argument parsing (valid, deduplicated and invalid forms), all three exit-code paths, `--now` replay stability, and the read-only assertion.

## Minimal implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.ts` — new CLI: `parseProvenanceAuditArgs`, `defaultProvenanceAuditCliIo`, `main(argv, io)` and the `--help` text, modelled line-for-line on `prep-supply-report-cli.ts`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.test.ts` — AC1/AC3/AC4 regressions with fully injected I/O (no live worklog, no `wl` subprocess); the read-only regression injects a seam whose every write surface throws if called and asserts the item/flag payload and the `<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` bytes are identical before and after a run.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — new `bin` entry plus the `chmod +x` extension in `build:only`.
- Reuse: `loadSettings` (`settings.ts`) with a locally resolved settings path, and the child 1/child 2 modules.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.ts` — new CLI entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit-cli.test.ts` — CLI regressions.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — `bin` + `build:only` chmod.
- `packages/herdr/src/prep-supply-report-cli.ts` — the template (unchanged).

## Constraints

- Strictly read-only, proven not asserted (AC4): no flag, assignee or marker mutation anywhere in the path.
- Fail closed: an unreadable root or unparseable payload is an error named on stderr with exit `1`, never an empty healthy row set.
- Deterministic ordering and rendering; no wall-clock leakage into the payload beyond `--now`/`now`.
- UK English in the usage text and output copy.
- Changed-scope suite must pass through `/skill:test` (never ad-hoc test invocations).

## Out of scope

Flag clearing, reassignment, batching producer interviews, and any dispatch/gate/skill behaviour change — those belong to other items (WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV, WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER).

## Dependencies

Blocked by the pure assembly (child 3) and its fixtures (child 1).

## Goal

Land the **test-first** slice of the provenance audit: the shared fixtures and regression harness that pin the behaviour the implementation slices must satisfy — above all that an inbound `depended-on-by` edge is never a hold.

Child 1 of 5 of WL-0MWTWQSN8005FK5P (child of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD). It is created and implemented before the read seam, the assembly and the CLI (test-first ordering), and its fixtures are consumed by those children's tests.

## User story

As a reviewer, I want the inbound-edge-vs-outbound-edge distinction and the read-only/replay contracts pinned as fixtures before any implementation exists, so that the implementation cannot pass by defining its own expectations.

## Context

- The 2026-11-23 recorded audit regraded `AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P` because six **inbound** `depended-on-by` edges were read as dependencies. Its only outbound edge pointed at a `completed` item, so no dependency hold existed. That specific shape must be a fixture.
- The dispatcher's hold vocabulary is `dependency`, `assignee-hold`, `startOn`, `attempt-budget`, `cooldown`, `dispatch-marker`.
- Terminal blocker statuses are `completed` and `deleted` (`TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts`); an unresolvable blocker status is treated as unmet (fail-closed).
- Fixtures must be **plain data with literal expectations** — no `expectedHolds()` helper that re-implements the predicates, because a second copy of the rule is exactly the drift this item exists to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new fixture module exposes named plain-data fixtures covering, at minimum: six inbound `depended-on-by` edges with one terminal outbound `depends-on` edge (expected hooks `[]`); one outbound `depends-on` edge to a non-terminal blocker (expected holds `['dependency']`); one outbound edge to a `completed` blocker and one to a `deleted` blocker (expected holds `[]`); an unresolvable blocker status (expected holds `['dependency']`, fail-closed); an `assignee` hold; a future `startOn`; an exhausted attempt budget at the current stage; an active non-terminal cooldown; and an outstanding stage-guard dispatch marker.
- Each fixture carries its expected hold tokens as **literal data** (for example `expectedHolds: ['dependency']`); no fixture expectation is computed by a function that restates a dispatcher predicate.
- A reusable read-only harness captures and compares the state the audit must not change: the item/flag payload for the roots plus the bytes of `<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, and reports whether they are byte-identical.
- A replay harness asserts that two serialisations produced at the same frozen instant are byte-identical, and that a differing instant changes only the age fields — expressed as a general helper, not tied to the not-yet-written modules.
- Every fixture and harness is unit-tested, and the module imports no production module that does not yet exist, so the change builds and its tests pass on its own.
- Tests are written first: this child's own tests exist before any child 2–4 source module is written.

## Minimal implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.fixtures.ts` — the fixture corpus and its literal expectations (playbook data only, no predicates).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.fixtures.test.ts` — unit tests asserting each fixture's shape and that expectations are literal data.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.harness.ts` — the read-only snapshot/diff and replay-stability helpers (pure; no `wl`, no filesystem writes).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.harness.test.ts` — harness unit tests.
- Reuse only types and constants that already exist: `ProducerReviewProvenanceInput` / `ProducerReviewVerdict`, `PRODUCER_REVIEW_SOURCES`, `PRODUCER_REVIEW_GROUPS`, `TERMINAL_STATUSES` semantics, and the `DowntimeLogEntry` shape.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.fixtures.ts` — fixture corpus with literal expected holds.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.fixtures.test.ts` — fixture unit tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.harness.ts` — read-only snapshot/diff + replay helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.provenance-audit.harness.test.ts` — harness unit tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.producer-review-provenance.ts` — reused types (unchanged).

## Constraints

- Plain data only: no I/O, no `wl`, no spawn, no filesystem access in the fixtures or harness.
- Expectations are literal — never derived by a helper that restates a gate predicate.
- Build gate: this child must build and pass its own tests in isolation, with no forward reference to children 2–4.
- UK English in comments, fixture names and docs.
- Changed-scope suite runs through `/skill:test`, never an ad-hoc invocation.

## Out of scope

Any production module (read seam, assembly, CLI) and the documentation section; those are children 2–5.

data.description:
# Soft-delete tombstone resurrects after `wl undelete`

Discovered from: WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 (see its comment `WL-C0MWUSER6L005TGRW`).

## Problem statement

A soft-deleted work item that was restored with `wl undelete` silently becomes
un-updatable again days later, because the JSONL sync merge/pull path lets a
stale copy of the tombstone (`deletedBy` / `deleteReason`) win over the cleared
restore. The visible symptom is a refused `wl update`; the only recovery is
another `wl undelete`.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** who restored an item with `wl undelete` and expects it
  to stay live — "As someone who recovered a retirement, I want the item to stay
  updatable after future syncs so I don't have to fix it again days later."
- **Agents running lifecycle skills** (implement / plan / audit) on a restored
  item — "As an agent, I want my work-item writes to keep succeeding after a
  sync so my session does not fail with a confusing soft-delete refusal."
- **Automation / scheduler** (dispatch, claims) that writes to restored items —
  "As automation, I want a live item to never be reported soft-deleted."

## Symptom (observed)

1. 2026-11-18T23:06Z — item soft-deleted by `Map`
   (`deleteReason: "Won't fix — operator decision."`).
2. 2026-11-19T00:27Z — `wl undelete` restored it (audit comment: "Restored from
   soft-delete via `wl undelete`. Previous status: blocked; deletedBy: Map;
   deleteReason: Won't fix — operator decision.. Restored to status: open.").
3. Work continued normally for days — child sessions completed, comments posted
   (2026-11-19 → 2026-11-23), a full audit ran (2026-11-20T04:54Z).
4. 2026-11-24T14:19Z — every lifecycle write failed with:

   ```
   Work item WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 is soft-deleted (deletedBy: Map) and cannot be updated.
   ```

   `wl show --json` still reported `deletedBy: "Map"`,
   `deleteReason: "Won't fix — operator decision."`, while status/stage carried
   live post-restore values. `wl undelete --dry-run` then reported
   `previousDeletedBy: Map` — the tombstone was **present again**.

## Impact

A restored item silently becomes un-updatable again, days later, with no
warning: the visible symptom is a refused `wl update`, and the only fix is
another `wl undelete`. Any automation (implement/plan/audit lifecycle writes,
scheduler claims) hitting the item simply fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A reproduction demonstrates the tombstone returning after `wl undelete`
   followed by a sync/merge cycle, committed as an automated regression test
   (not only a written report). The sequence must mirror the incident — a
   restore, then a later pull/merge against a snapshot that still carries
   `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` (including the delta-sync and repeated/multi-peer
   interleavings the existing two-store test does not exercise).
2. `wl undelete` (with its auto-sync) leaves the item permanently updatable
   across a subsequent full **and** delta `wl sync` round-trip; a regression
   test asserts repeated syncs never reinstate a non-empty `deletedBy` and that a
   following `wl update` succeeds.
3. The merge/pull path treats a cleared tombstone as authoritative: once a live
   copy with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` is the reconciled winner, a stale
   snapshot can never reinstate a non-empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`; covered
   by a merge-level regression test.
4. A restored item's `wl show --json` never reports a non-empty `deletedBy`
   while its `status` is live (invariant asserted in the regression test).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably the
   restore/tombstone rules in `DATA_SYNCING.md`).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No schema or JSONL field changes.** The restore stays represented by the
  cleared attribution plus a newer `updatedAt` (documented in
  `DATA_SYNCING.md`).
- **Preserve delete-side protection.** Unattributed deletes (`deletedBy` and
  `deleteReason` both empty) must never override a live copy; a later attributed
  delete must still win; at equal timestamps the tombstone keeps winning
  (existing deliberate rule).
- **Recency still decides.** The fix must not make an item undeletable or
  resurrect an item against a genuinely newer delete.
- **Cover both sync kinds.** Full snapshots and the delta export/import path must
  both converge, since the incident spanned days of syncing.
- **Do not regress** `tests/sync/undelete-merge.test.ts` or
  `tests/cli/undelete-sync-roundtrip.test.ts`.

## Existing state

- `wl undelete` (`src/commands/undelete.ts`) clears `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`
  through `db.update`, which bumps `updatedAt`, records an audit comment, then
  auto-syncs once.
- Merge reconciliation (`src/sync/field-merge.ts`) already carries a
  `restoreSide` rule for `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`; the same-timestamp path
  deliberately lets a tombstone win ties.
- `db.import()` / `db.upsertItems()` (`packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts`)
  re-stamp `updatedAt` on a semantic change and skip no-op saves.
- `isSoftDeleted(item)` is `status === 'deleted' || deletedBy non-empty`, so the
  observed "live status + leftover `deletedBy`" is exactly a soft-delete state.
- The existing unit merge tests and the two-store round-trip test pass, yet the
  incident recurred days later — so the current coverage does not reach the
  failing path (likely delta sync, repeated/multi-peer interleaving, or a
  persist/re-stamp gap).

## Desired change

Identify and fix the path (merge/pull resolution, delta export/import, or
persist) that lets a stale tombstone win over a cleared restore, add the
reproduction and regression tests above, and document the authoritative-clear
rule.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/undelete.ts` — restore write, audit comment, auto-sync.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — delete attribution, status/stage semantics.
- `src/sync/field-merge.ts` — `mergeRemoteItem`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`,
  `mergeSameTimestampItems` (`restoreSide` handling).
- `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` — `isAttributedDelete` and related predicates.
- `src/sync/merge.ts` — `mergeWorkItems` entry point.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — pull → merge → persist → delta-export pipeline.
- `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts` — `import()` / `upsertItems()`
  `updatedAt` re-stamp and no-op guard.
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` — `update()`, `deleteSingle()`,
  `isSoftDeleted()`.
- `tests/sync/undelete-merge.test.ts`, `tests/cli/undelete-sync-roundtrip.test.ts`
  — existing coverage to extend.
- `DATA_SYNCING.md` — restore/tombstone merge rules to update.

## Related work

Potentially related work items:

- **WL-0MWMRNL2W003W5R3** – Add `wl undelete` so a soft-deleted item can be
  recovered (completed) — introduced the restore semantics this bug undermines.
- **WL-0MWMS48UG005CUBN** – Implement the shared database restore helper
  (completed) — `db.update` restore path that clears the tombstone.
- **WL-0MWMS4GUJ00576TB** – Test-first: restore vs tombstone merge
  reconciliation (completed) — the merge unit tests.
- **WL-0MWMS4J2Z00215JL** – Implement merge reconciliation for restore
  (completed) — the `restoreSide` merge rule.
- **WL-0MWMS4LRR003N608** – Recover epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 with the new
  command (completed) — the restore whose convergence failed.
- **WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG** – Regression tests: sync convergence + delete
  protection (completed).
- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** – Dispatcher seems to unevenly distribute work
  (blocked) — the item the tombstone resurrected on; discovery source.
- Related code references: `WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO` (delete-side protection),
  `WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE` (deletion propagation).

Potentially related docs:

- `DATA_SYNCING.md` — merge rules incl. "Restoring a Soft-Deleted Item".
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — sync mechanics.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatch/lifecycle write context.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** an over-eager "cleared tombstone always wins" could resurrect an item
  against a genuinely newer delete. Mitigation: keep recency and the
  equal-timestamp tombstone tie-break intact; only the *reconciled winner* is
  authoritative.
- **Risk:** the root cause may be delta-export propagation (the restore never
  reaches peers) rather than merge resolution; the fix may belong in dirty
  tracking/export. Investigation must confirm which path fails before patching.
- **Risk:** `wl undelete` auto-sync failures are swallowed (warning only), which
  can leave the remote tombstoned. Surfacing that harder is adjacent scope — if
  needed, record as a linked follow-up rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption (scope):** the fix targets the merge/pull/export path plus
  regression coverage; read-time self-healing (auto-clearing a tombstone on
  `wl show`/`wl list`) is **out of scope** unless the merge fix proves
  insufficient — then record it as a follow-up.
- **Assumption (reproduction):** an automated reproduction is feasible with the
  existing two-store harness by adding a stale full snapshot and/or delta
  interleaving; if the exact incident cannot be reproduced, the closest
  reproducible analogue plus a test that fails against current behaviour is
  acceptable (AC1), not a bare "could not reproduce" note.
- **Scope-creep guard:** extra hardening discovered along the way is captured as
  linked work items, not folded into this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Who is the primary user affected?**
  Answer (research): producers/operators who run `wl undelete`, agents whose
  lifecycle writes hit the restored item, and scheduler/dispatch automation.
  Source: incident symptom, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

- **Q: Do the existing undelete sync tests already cover this?**
  Answer (research): No. `tests/sync/undelete-merge.test.ts` proves the merge
  rule in isolation and `tests/cli/undelete-sync-roundtrip.test.ts` proves the
  two-store happy path; the incident recurred days later, so the failing path
  (delta sync / repeated multi-peer interleaving / persist re-stamp) is not
  covered. Source: read both test files.

- **Q: Is the suspected cause confirmed?**
  Answer (research): Not yet. The item lists two hypotheses — a
  last-writer-wins merge on a stale snapshot, or an undelete whose clear is not
  synced so a later pull lets the stale `deletedBy` win. Reproduction is the
  first task. Source: item "Suspected cause".

- **Q: Should the fix add read-time self-healing?**
  Answer (assumption, not blocking): No — narrow the fix to the
  merge/pull/export path plus regression tests; add self-healing only if the
  merge fix proves insufficient, then as a linked follow-up. Source: scope-creep
  guard above.

- **Q: Must reproduction be a committed automated test?**
  Answer (assumption, not blocking): Yes — AC1 requires an automated regression
  test, consistent with the work-item conventions. Source: AC list above.

# Test-first: reproduce stale-tombstone resurrection

Parent: WL-0MWUSJTZN000MXTF.

## Goal

Commit an automated reproduction of the incident: a restored item (live
`status`, empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`, newer `updatedAt`) meets a stale
snapshot that still carries the tombstone, and the tombstone comes back. The
reproduction must also identify *which* path actually fails (merge resolution,
delta persist, or repeated interleaving) before any fix lands.

## Context

- Merge rules live in `src/sync/field-merge.ts`. `restoreSide` is only set
  inside the `status` branch, and only when the losing side's status is exactly
  `deleted` *and* attributed. Otherwise `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` fall through
  to the default-vs-value rule, where a stale non-empty attribution beats a
  cleared one regardless of recency.
- Persist path: `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts` re-stamps
  `updatedAt` to *now* on a semantic change in both `import()` (full snapshot)
  and `upsertItems()` (delta).
- Delta export is driven by an `updatedAt > watermark` dirty check
  (`packages/shared/src/database/sync.ts` → `countDirtyRecords`).
- Existing coverage: `tests/sync/undelete-merge.test.ts` (unit merge rules) and
  `tests/cli/undelete-sync-roundtrip.test.ts` (one two-store happy path). Both
  pass today, so neither reaches the failing path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new automated test file reproduces the resurrection: after a
  `wl undelete`-equivalent restore, a merge/persist against a stale snapshot
  carrying `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` must leave the item with empty
  `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; the assertion fails against current `HEAD`
  and the red-first output is recorded in a comment on this item.
- The reproduction exercises all three suspected paths — a stale full snapshot,
  a stale delta payload (`upsertItems`), and a repeated three-cycle sync loop —
  and names the path that actually fails in a comment, with the failing
  assertion quoted.
- A reusable invariant assertion "a live `status` never coexists with a
  non-empty `deletedBy`" is asserted on the merged and persisted result (fails
  before the fix, passes after it).
- No test is left skipped or `test.fails`-marked in the final state, and
  `tests/sync/undelete-merge.test.ts` plus
  `tests/cli/undelete-sync-roundtrip.test.ts` remain unmodified and green.
- Parent AC (restated so the tree-coverage review can trace it): a reproduction demonstrates the tombstone returning after `wl undelete` followed by a sync/merge cycle, committed as an automated regression test (not only a written report). The sequence must mirror the incident — a restore, then a later pull/merge against a snapshot that still carries `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` (including the delta-sync and repeated/multi-peer interleavings the existing two-store test does not exercise).

# Fix: cleared tombstone authoritative in merge

Parent: WL-0MWUSJTZN000MXTF.

## Goal

Make a reconciled live winner's cleared attribution authoritative in the merge:
once the winning side is live with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`, a stale
non-empty attribution can never be copied back.

## Context

`mergeDifferentTimestampItems` sets `restoreSide` only inside the `status`
branch, and only when the losing side's status is exactly `deleted` and
attributed. When both sides carry the same live `status`, or the stale copy
carries the attribution without `status: 'deleted'`, `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`
fall through to the default-vs-value rule: local `''` is a default, remote
`'Map'` is not, so the tombstone attribution wins *regardless of recency*. That
produces exactly the observed hybrid — live status/stage with a resurrected
`deletedBy`. `mergeSameTimestampItems` has no `restoreSide` equivalent at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `deletedBy` and `deleteReason` follow the reconciled live winner whenever the
  winner has an empty attribution — including when both sides carry the same
  live `status`, and when the losing copy's `status` is not `deleted`.
- A later attributed delete still wins by recency, and an equal-timestamp
  divergence still resolves to the tombstone (the deliberate tie-break is
  unchanged).
- Unattributed deletes still never override a live copy — delete-side
  protection (`WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO`) is untouched and its tests stay green.
- Merge-level regression tests in `tests/sync/undelete-merge.test.ts` (or the
  reproduction file from the test-first child) cover the failing path and
  assert `deletedBy === ''` and `deleteReason === ''` on the merged result.
- No schema, JSONL field or public-API change — `git diff` touches no field
  definitions in `src/types.ts` or `packages/shared/src/types.ts`.
- Parent AC (restated so the tree-coverage review can trace it): the merge/pull path treats a cleared tombstone as authoritative — once a live copy with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` is the reconciled winner, a stale snapshot can never reinstate a non-empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`; covered by a merge-level regression test.


## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the `restoreSide` concept in `src/sync/field-merge.ts` into an
  attribution rule that applies to both the differing-timestamp and
  same-timestamp paths.
- Add or reuse a predicate in `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` (e.g. "winner is
  live and unattributed") so the rule is testable in isolation.
- Leave the existing `status` branch semantics untouched; only the attribution
  fields gain the winner-follows rule.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the test-first reproduction child (its root-cause finding decides
whether this child or the sync-convergence child owns the fix).

**Key Files:**

- `src/sync/field-merge.ts`
- `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts`
- `src/sync/merge.ts`
- `tests/sync/undelete-merge.test.ts`

# Fix: full and delta sync convergence

Parent: WL-0MWUSJTZN000MXTF.

## Goal

Guarantee that after `wl undelete` the restored item stays live across a
subsequent full **and** delta `wl sync` round-trip, so no stale snapshot and no
repeated interleaving can re-tombstone it.

## Context

`src/commands/sync.ts` pulls, merges, then persists: `db.import()` for a full
snapshot and `db.upsertItems()` for a delta. Both re-stamp `updatedAt` to *now*
on any semantic change (`packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts`), which
can make a stale tombstone look like the newest write, and delta export is
driven by an `updatedAt > watermark` dirty check. The incident spanned days of
syncing, so the failing path may be persist/export rather than merge resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/cli/undelete-sync-roundtrip.test.ts` (or a new CLI test) extends the
  two-store round-trip with a **delta** `wl sync` while the peer still holds the
  stale tombstone; the restored item ends live with `deletedBy === ''` and
  `deleteReason === ''`.
- Three or more consecutive sync cycles between the two stores never reinstate a
  non-empty `deletedBy`, and a `wl update` on the restored item succeeds after
  the final cycle.
- A full-snapshot round-trip asserts the same convergence.
- If the reproduction shows the persist/export path is at fault, the fix lands
  there (re-stamp or dirty-watermark handling) with no schema change and no
  change to watermark semantics; if the merge fix alone suffices, a regression
  test still pins the delta path so it cannot silently regress.
- `wl show --json` after the round-trip reports a live `status` with empty
  `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`.
- Parent AC (restated so the tree-coverage review can trace it): `wl undelete` (with its auto-sync) leaves the item permanently updatable across a subsequent full **and** delta `wl sync` round-trip; a regression test asserts repeated syncs never reinstate a non-empty `deletedBy` and that a following `wl update` succeeds.
- Parent AC (restated so the tree-coverage review can trace it): a restored item's `wl show --json` never reports a non-empty `deletedBy` while its `status` is live (invariant asserted in the regression test).
- Parent AC (restated so the tree-coverage review can trace it): the full project test suite must pass with the new changes (run through the test skill; the dev-push gate enforces it).


## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the existing real-git-remote harness; drive `wl sync` in both
  directions per cycle (peer A ↔ peer B).
- Re-read via `wl show --json`, assert on the JSON fields, then run a
  `wl update` as the end-to-end check.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the test-first reproduction child and the merge-fix child.

- `src/commands/sync.ts`
