# Add a table for acceptance criteria (ACs)

## Original request (verbatim)

> At present the acceptance criteria of a work item is embedded in the
> description of the item. Add a separate table that will capture the
> acceptance criteria, 1 row per record. The table will contain, at least, an
> ID, the owning work item id, the description of the criteria and a status
> (met, unmet, partial, modified) and (if modified) a textual description of
> the original AC and the justification for the change made in the current AC
> description. An acceptance criteria for this work item will be that all
> ../SorraAgent skills that work with acceptance criteria are modified to use
> this table rather than the text embedded in the description. A second AC will
> be that wl doctor, when upgradeing to this new db version, will iterate over
> all work items that have not been deleted and migrate their ACs to this new
> structure. A thid AC will be that the CLI has `wl ac add/delete/update/show/search`
> commands (show will show the AC for a given work item, search will search
> return the ACs and their owning work items that match a search string).
> Another AC will be that there is a new high priority work item in
> ../SorraAgents to update the relevant skills (at least find related and
> implement) to use these ACs rather than a full `wl show` where possible.

## Problem statement

A work item's acceptance criteria live as free-text prose inside
`workitems.description`. Every consumer therefore re-parses that prose with its
own regex, there is no identity or status for an individual criterion, and no
way to record that a criterion was re-worded (or why). Add a first-class
`acceptance_criteria` table so each criterion is a row with a stable id, its
own status, and a preserved record of the original wording when it changes.

## Users

- **Agent (implement / plan / audit skills)** — "I want to read a work item's
  criteria as structured rows so I do not have to regex the description, and I
  want to see each criterion's status instead of inferring it."
- **Agent or producer reviewing a change** — "I want to see which criteria are
  met, unmet, partial or modified — and for modified ones, what the original
  said and why it changed."
- **Operator (downtime dispatcher / standups / reporting)** — "I want to query
  'which criteria mention X' across the whole worklog and get back the owning
  item, not grep 4,800 descriptions."

Example user stories:

- As an implementing agent, I read AC rows for my work item and address them in
  order, marking each `met` as I complete it.
- As an auditor, I mark a criterion `modified` and record the original wording
  plus the justification, so the deviation is visible in `wl ac show`.
- As an operator, I run `wl ac search "full project test suite"` and get every
  criterion that carries the boilerplate clause plus its owning item.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Data model and persistence

- A new `acceptance_criteria` table exists in the SQLite schema with, at least,
  an AC id, the owning work item id (FK to `workitems(id)`, `ON DELETE
  CASCADE`), the criterion text, a status constrained to `met|unmet|partial|
  modified`, a stable ordering column, and — for `modified` rows — the original
  criterion text and the justification for the change; `SCHEMA_VERSION`
  (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`) and `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`
  (`src/migrations/index.ts`) are bumped together by exactly one step.
- AC rows round-trip through JSONL export/import and Git sync as their own
  record type: a full export → import into an empty store reproduces every row
  exactly (text, status, ordering, original + justification), and a delta sync
  between an ahead and a behind store carries AC additions, updates and
  deletions without dropping the behind store's other rows.

### Migration (`wl doctor upgrade`)

- A migration under `src/migrations/index.ts` iterates every **non-deleted**
  work item that has an `## Acceptance Criteria` section, inserts one row per
  criterion in document order, and is idempotent — re-running creates no
  duplicate rows, and deleted work items yield zero rows.
- The back-fill and the strip are **two separately-runnable migrations**, not
  one atomic step, so the strip can be sequenced after
  `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` lands: the second migration removes the
  `## Acceptance Criteria` section from every migrated description (the table
  becomes the sole source of truth — producer decision Q1 = A), is idempotent
  and re-runnable, leaves every other description section untouched, and
  records each stripped item so a partially applied run can be resumed.
- Both migrations report a summary (items scanned, criteria inserted,
  descriptions stripped, items skipped/unparseable) and `--dry-run` prints the
  same counts without writing; both are classified `safe: true` and run inside
  the existing single transaction.
- The audit content fingerprint moves to **schema 3** over
  `title` + `description` + the item's **ordered AC rows** (id, position, text,
  status), so an edit to a criterion invalidates a stored audit exactly as a
  description edit does today; schema-2 digests are treated as stale, and the
  bounded re-audit wave (358 stored fingerprints on this store, mostly old
  completed items) is surfaced by `wl doctor` rather than silently absorbed.

### CLI

- `wl ac add`, `wl ac delete`, `wl ac update`, `wl ac show` and `wl ac search`
  exist and behave per this contract: `show <work-item-id>` lists that item's
  criteria in document order with their status; `search <text>` returns
  matching criteria **and** their owning work item id + title; all five support
  `--json` and non-zero exit codes for unknown ids and invalid arguments.
- `wl ac` is registered in `src/command-registry.ts`, appears in grouped
  `wl --help` output and in shell completion, and `wl show <id>` renders the
  item's criteria from the table so a consumer needs no second query.

### Cross-repo and compatibility

- The cross-repo item is the recorded blocker: **`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`**
  (*Use the worklog acceptance-criteria table instead of parsing AC prose*,
  `high`, `open`, `../SorraAgents`) switches the skills that parse AC prose (at
  least `find-related` and `implement`, plus the shared `tree_coverage.py`
  extraction) onto the table, and the dependency edge
  `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` is recorded in this store, so
  this item cannot reach `in_review` until that item completes (producer
  decision Q2 = C). This item documents the compatibility contract that keeps
  the current description-based parse working until that item lands.
- The fingerprint schema bump ships **in lockstep** with
  `../SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
  (`_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA`, `_compute_content_fingerprint`): the
  parity check is fail-on-skew
  (`src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts`, `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts`),
  so a one-sided bump turns `dev` red and a one-sided digest makes every audit
  read stale. The transition must accept a declared-schema **set** (the union of
  the old and new version) on both sides until both repositories have shipped.
- AC status is **advisory** in this delivery (producer decision Q3 = A): no
  gate — `wl next`, `worklist`, `audit`, `doctor`, or any skill — may block,
  warn or otherwise branch on AC status; statuses are stored, rendered and
  queryable only.

### Testing, docs and validation

- Characterisation tests cover the migration against a real-world fixture of
  the AC shapes actually present in the worklog (checkbox `- [ ]`, bold-led,
  period- and paren-numbered, hard-wrapped multi-line, nested sub-bullets), and
  prove extraction parity with
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` for the same
  text.
- Changed-scope tests cover CLI CRUD + exit codes, JSONL round-trip, and
  migration idempotence.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, `README`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Acceptance criteria become addressable rows with their own status — so an agent
or reviewer can see at a glance which criteria are met, unmet, partial or
modified (and, where re-worded, what it said before and why) instead of parsing
prose out of a work item's description.

## Scope notes (detail for the plan stage, not parent-level ACs)

- **AC ids** follow the existing worklog id-generator convention with a
  position-stable, human-recognisable form, so ids survive reordering and never
  collide with work-item or comment ids (`WL-C0…` is the comment namespace).
- **Ordering** is an explicit integer column (not lexical id order) so a
  criterion can be inserted or reordered without renumbering the rest.
- **Status maintenance is manual in this item** (`wl ac update --status`), and
  status is **advisory**: by producer decision (Q3 = A) no gate consults it —
  it is stored, rendered and queryable only. The audit skill already emits a
  per-criterion verdict table using the vocabulary
  `met|unmet|partial|adjusted` (`skill/audit/SKILL.md` § "Acceptance Criteria
  Status"), and `adjusted` ≈ `modified`. Wiring `persist_audit.py` to write
  those verdicts into the table is a natural follow-up but is **out of scope
  here** — it changes the audit pipeline's contract and belongs in its own
  work item (see "Related work / discovered opportunities").
- **`wl ac search`** reuses the existing search plumbing (`worklog_fts` where
  it covers the new table, otherwise a `LIKE` fallback with the same ordering
  semantics); the choice is an implementation detail for the plan stage.
- **Read cache**: AC writes must invalidate the read cache entry for the owning
  work item so `wl show` never serves a stale criterion list.

## Constraints

- Additive migration only on existing databases; no destructive rewrite of
  `workitems`. Migration policy: `docs/DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`,
  `docs/migrations.md`.
- The `wl` CLI fast path (`src/cli.ts`) has a hard startup-import budget
  (`tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`); the new command module must load
  through the heavy graph (`src/command-registry.ts` loader map), not the fast
  path.
- `../SorraAgents` is a separate repository with its own release pipeline —
  skill changes there must not be made from this repository's worktree.
- Write in UK English; documentation only, `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the
  ship pipeline.

## Existing state

- ACs are prose in `workitems.description` under an `## Acceptance Criteria`
  heading. Parsing is duplicated: the canonical parser is
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` (dash `-`,
  plus `+`, `1.` and `1)` markers; nested deeper-indented markers are detail,
  not criteria; hard-wrapped continuations are joined; `*` star bullets are
  **not** recognised). `src/` (TypeScript) does **not** parse ACs at all —
  the only `src/` reference is a comment in `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`.
- Measured against this store (`.worklog/worklog.db`, read-only inspection):

  | Measure | Count |
  |---|---|
  | Work items | 4,865 |
  | Deleted work items | 376 |
  | Items with an `## Acceptance Criteria` section | 3,020 |
  | Items whose section parses to ≥ 1 criterion | 2,588 |
  | Criteria parseable today | 15,172 |
  | … written as checkbox `- [ ]` | 3,103 (61 ticked) |
  | … with bold markers | 2,525 |
  | … plain text | 9,962 |
  | Stored audit fingerprints | 358 (of 2,600 audit rows) |

  Checkbox state is **not** a usable status signal (61 ticked of 3,103), so
  migrated criteria default to `unmet` rather than inferring from `[x]`.
- The audit content fingerprint (`src/audit-fingerprint.ts`, schema 2) hashes
  `title` + `description`; the description "carries the acceptance criteria",
  so moving criteria out of the description changes what the fingerprint
  covers — hence the schema-3 bump (Q1 = A). The `../SorraAgents` audit skill
  implements the same digest behind a fail-on-skew parity check
  (`_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2`), so the two move together.
- Schema version is a paired constant: `SCHEMA_VERSION = 10` in
  `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` and
  `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = '10'` in `src/migrations/index.ts`; the most recent
  comparable data-model slice is `WL-0MWMGEPY2004EDZ8` (`startOn`), which is
  the template for "column + migration + doctor check + JSONL round-trip".

## Desired change

1. Schema + migration for `acceptance_criteria`, version bump, JSONL/sync
   support, read-cache invalidation.
2. `wl doctor upgrade` migrations that back-fill one row per criterion from
   every non-deleted work item's description and then strip the
   `## Acceptance Criteria` section (two separately-runnable steps),
   idempotently, with dry-run counts and a summary; plus the audit fingerprint
   schema-3 bump over the ordered AC rows.
3. `wl ac add|delete|update|show|search` plus `wl show` rendering from the
   table.
4. Docs, tests, and a cross-repo high-priority `../SorraAgents` work item for
   the skill switch.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — needs the `acceptance_criteria`
  DDL, indexes, `REQUIRED_TABLES` entry and the `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (+ `database/`) — needs AC CRUD methods
  (add/list/update/delete/search) alongside the existing comment methods.
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — needs the new entry (table creation + back-fill)
  and the matching `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump.
- `src/commands/ac.ts` — **new** — registers `wl ac add|delete|update|show|search`.
- `src/command-registry.ts` — needs `ac` in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES` and
  `COMMAND_LOADERS`.
- `src/commands/show.ts` — needs the AC section rendered from the table.
- `src/jsonl.ts` — needs the new `acceptance_criterion` record type in export
  and import.
- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — needs the schema-3 payload over ordered AC rows,
  plus `src/list-enrichment.ts` and `src/commands/update.ts` call sites that
  pass only title/description today.
- `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts` + `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts`
  — need declared-schema-set acceptance for the lockstep transition.
- `src/read-cache*.ts` — needs AC writes to invalidate the owning item's cache.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — needs the `AcceptanceCriterion` type and
  status union.
- `CLI.md`, `DATA_FORMAT.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` (repository root, not
  `docs/`), `docs/migrations.md`, `docs/dev/acceptance-criteria.md` (new) —
  needs the contract documented.
- `packages/shared/src/acceptance-criteria.ts` (new) — the TypeScript AC
  extractor the back-fill migration uses, guarded by a parity test.
- `tests/cli/ac-*.test.ts`, `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-*.test.ts`,
  `tests/fixtures/acceptance-criteria/` — **new** — CLI, migration, extraction
  and round-trip coverage.
- `../SorraAgents/skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — reference only for
  extraction parity; the behavioural switch lives in the cross-repo item.

## Related work

- `WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` — *Cross-repo dependency edges are silently dropped by
  the sync prefix filter* — critical bug found while completing this intake; it
  is a prerequisite here because the Q2 = C blocker cannot be enforced while
  foreign-target edges vanish on sync.
- `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` (cross-repo, `../SorraAgents`) — *Use the worklog
  acceptance-criteria table instead of parsing AC prose* — created by this
  intake per producer decision Q2 = C and recorded as this item's blocker.
- `WL-0MWMGEPY2004EDZ8` — *`startOn` data model, schema migration and sync
  round-trip* — the closest structural precedent (column + migration + doctor
  check + JSONL round-trip); follow its shape and its `doctor` mismatch check.
- `WL-0MVO93BBC000H734` — *tree_coverage AC extraction ignores
  numbered acceptance-criteria lists* — established the canonical AC marker
  rules the migration must match.
- `WL-0MWHWOED6004EXFW` — *Close coverage gap: AC4* — one of the many
  auto-generated "close coverage gap" items that exist purely because prose
  ACs cannot be matched reliably; a concrete measure of the machinery this item
  replaces.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `extract_acceptance_criteria`,
  `compute_coverage`, `apply_coverage_review`.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` § "Acceptance Criteria Status" — the existing
  per-criterion verdict vocabulary (`met|unmet|partial|adjusted`).
- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` + `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` — the
  description-hash contract affected by Q1.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — audit-fingerprint invalidation (Q1 = A, accepted).** Stripping the
  AC section changes every affected description, and the schema-3 bump makes
  schema-2 digests unmatchable, so the 358 stored fingerprints go stale and
  those items re-enter the audit gate. Accepted deliberately; mitigated by
  surfacing the wave in `wl doctor` with the affected id list before the strip
  runs, so the re-audit cost is scheduled rather than discovered.
- **Risk — dual source of truth.** A table plus a description section will
  disagree unless one is declared authoritative and the other generated or
  removed. This is exactly Q1.
- **Risk — skills break once the strip lands.** Every SorraAgents skill that
  regexes the description sees no criteria after the second landing. Mitigated
  by the three-step delivery sequence above: the strip is the last step and is
  blocked by `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`, so the skills read the table before the
  prose disappears.
- **Risk — fingerprint lockstep.** A one-sided schema bump either turns `dev`
  red (parity test fail-on-skew) or makes every audit read stale. Mitigation:
  accept the declared-schema set on both sides for the transition window.
- **Risk — 15k-row migration on a live store.** Measure the run time, keep it
  in the existing single transaction with a pre-upgrade backup, and prove
  idempotence on a copy of this store.
- **Risk — parse drift.** A second AC parser (TypeScript) can diverge from
  `tree_coverage.py`; the parity test is the guard.
- **Assumption — default status `unmet`.** Checkbox state is not a status
  signal (61 of 3,103 ticked), so migrated rows start `unmet`.
- **Assumption — statuses are maintained manually in this item** and are
  **advisory** (Q3 = A): no gate consults them; audit verdict sync is a
  follow-up work item.
- **Delivery sequence (Q1 = A + Q2 = C, the compatibility contract).** Two
  landings, because the two decisions interlock — the skills switch needs the
  `wl ac` CLI from this item, and this item is blocked by the skills switch:
  1. **This item, first landing** — table, back-fill migration (descriptions
     untouched), `wl ac` CLI, `wl show` rendering, JSONL/sync, docs. Pushed to
     `dev`; descriptions still carry their AC sections, so every existing skill
     keeps working unchanged.
  2. **`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`** — skills read the table (description parse kept
     as a documented fallback for unmigrated stores).
  3. **This item, second landing** — the strip migration + fingerprint schema 3
     (in lockstep with the SorraAgents audit skill), then `in_review`.
  The apparent dependency cycle is resolved by landing the back-fill without the
  strip; nothing in the interim depends on criteria living in two places being
  consistent, because the table is written first and the strip only removes
  text that is already represented as rows.
- **Assumption — AC ids use the existing generator** (position-stable, not
  derived from position).
- **Scope creep — search/reporting features.** Rich AC querying (filters by
  status across the tree, standup aggregation) is attractive but out of scope;
  record as discovered work items rather than widening this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (ANSWERED — producer decision): *After migration, where does the
  text of the criteria live?* Options: **(a)** the section is removed from the
  description so the table is the single source of truth — every affected
  description changes, invalidating the 358 stored audit fingerprints, so the
  fingerprint schema must also cover AC rows and those items need re-auditing;
  **(b)** the section stays in the description as a generated, read-only mirror
  of the table — no fingerprint churn, but two representations that can drift;
  **(c)** descriptions are left untouched and the table is a snapshot copy —
  cheapest, but the two diverge from the first AC edit.
  **Recommended: (a)** — it is the only option that actually removes the prose
  source of truth the skills currently depend on, and the re-audit wave is
  bounded (358 fingerprints, mostly old completed items).
  — Follow-up question (producer, 2026-11-26): *"Would C leave the audit
  fingerprints intact?"* — **Answer (agent, repo research): yes today, but only
  while AC edits stay invisible to audit freshness.** The fingerprint is
  `sha256(canonicalJson({schema: 2, title_hash, description_hash}))`
  (`src/audit-fingerprint.ts:402` `computeContentFingerprint`,
  `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2`; callers pass only `title` +
  `description` — `src/list-enrichment.ts:106`). Option C never rewrites a
  description, so all 358 stored digests still match and **no re-audit wave is
  triggered by the migration itself** — the one concrete advantage C has over
  (a). The cost: an AC edit via `wl ac update` (or an audit marking a criterion
  `modified`) changes neither title nor description, so the fingerprint does not
  move and an audit of the *old* wording still reads **fresh**. That defeats the
  stated purpose of the fingerprint, which exists because "the description
  carries the acceptance criteria" (`src/audit-fingerprint.ts:21`). Closing the
  gap means adding AC rows to the payload → schema 3 → every schema-2 digest
  becomes unmatchable → all 358 go stale at once, i.e. exactly the re-audit
  wave (a) pays for, merely deferred to whenever that bump lands. So C is
  viable as **C + keep schema 2 + a follow-up item for AC-aware fingerprints**,
  accepting the freshness gap in the interim (and accepting that any skill
  still regexing the description reads criteria frozen at migration time).
  — Answer (producer, 2026-11-26): **(a)** — strip the section, the table is the
  sole source of truth; accept the fingerprint bump and the resulting re-audit
  wave. Source: interactive reply, given after the C/fingerprint trade-off
  above was quantified. Consequences recorded as ACs and constraints below:
  the strip is a *second, separately-runnable* migration so it can be sequenced
  after `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`; the audit fingerprint schema moves to 3 over the
  ordered AC rows; and that bump must ship in lockstep with the `../SorraAgents`
  audit skill or the parity test goes red.

- Q2 (ANSWERED — producer decision): *Is the SorraAgents skill migration
  in scope for this item?* The original description contains both "all
  ../SorraAgent skills that work with acceptance criteria are modified to use
  this table" and "there is a new high priority work item in ../SorraAgents to
  update the relevant skills" — which are alternatives, not both. Options:
  **(a)** this item ships ContextHub only and creates the SorraAgents item;
  **(b)** this item ships ContextHub *and* the SorraAgents skill changes before
  it is marked in_review; **(c)** create the SorraAgents item and record it as
  a blocker so this item cannot be marked in_review until it lands.
  **Recommended: (a)** — one repository per item keeps review and release
  pipelines clean, and the item's own AC only requires that the SorraAgents
  item *exists*. Note the coupling: with Q1=(a) the description-backed skills
  break immediately, which makes (c) the safer pairing.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-11-26): **(c)** — create the SorraAgents item and
  record it as a blocker. Source: interactive reply. Evidence: created
  `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` (`high`, `open`, `../SorraAgents`) and recorded the
  cross-repo edge `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` (`wl dep add`),
  so this item is blocked from `in_review` until that item completes.

- Q3 (ANSWERED — producer decision): *Does AC status gate anything in
  phase 1?* Options: **(a)** advisory only — statuses are visible in
  `wl ac show` / `wl show` but no gate consults them; **(b)** a hard gate —
  an item cannot reach `in_review` while any criterion is `unmet`/`partial`;
  **(c)** a soft gate — the audit gate warns on `unmet` criteria but does not
  block.
  **Recommended: (a)** — 15,172 back-filled criteria default to `unmet`, so a
  hard gate would block essentially the whole board on day one.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-11-26): **(a)** advisory only. Source: interactive
  reply. Recorded as a constraint in "Cross-repo and compatibility" and as an
  assumption in "Risks and assumptions"; the follow-up audit-verdict sync item
  inherits the same advisory rule.

- Q4 (routine — settled by repo research): *Which AC markup must the migration
  understand?* — Answer (agent): dash `-`, plus `+`, `1.` and `1)` markers in
  document order, with deeper-indented markers treated as nested detail and
  hard-wrapped continuation lines joined; `*` star bullets are not recognised.
  Source: `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` and
  `WL-0MVO93BBC000H734`.

- Q5 (routine — settled by repo research): *What default status do migrated
  criteria get?* — Answer (agent): `unmet`. Source: measured this store —
  61 ticked vs 3,042 unticked checkboxes, so box state carries no signal.

- Q6 (routine — settled by repo research): *Which work item is the structural
  template?* — Answer (agent): `WL-0MWMGEPY2004EDZ8` (`startOn`), the most
  recent data-model slice (column, paired schema-version bump, migration,
  `doctor` mismatch check, JSONL round-trip).

- Q7 (routine — settled by repo research): *Does the TypeScript side already
  parse acceptance criteria?* — Answer (agent): no; only
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (Python) does. The new table needs a single
  TypeScript extraction path for the migration, guarded by a parity test
  against the Python implementation.

## Related work (automated report)

> Generated by `/skill:find-related`. The curated "Related work" section above is
> authoritative; this automated sweep matched largely on common words
> ("acceptance", "add", "change") and its three hits are low-signal — recorded
> for traceability only.

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6** – Remove unused WorkItem import from index.ts (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR51JO0037ISJ** – Eliminate unsafe as any casts in shortcut dispatch (detail view and duck-typing) (completed)
- **WL-0MKRRZ2DN1M2289R** – wl show is not showing human readable output (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: acceptance, add, another, capture, change (+50 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, add, another, capture, change (+50 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, another, capture, change, cli (+45 more)





## Plan (generated by `/skill:plan`, 2026-11-26)

Eleven child work items, ordered test-first, each a minimal end-to-end slice
(schema/behaviour + its tests + its docs note). Dependency edges are recorded in
this store; `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` is a foreign (cross-repo) blocker on both
landing-2 items.

| # | Child | Type | Priority | Depends on | Landing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `WL-0MWXJGRML004YI6O` AC extraction parity harness | task | medium | — | 1 |
| 2 | `WL-0MWXJGTPD006MZ3R` AC status advisory guard | task | medium | 5 | 1 |
| 3 | `WL-0MWXJGVOQ0068QWK` acceptance_criteria schema and version bump | feature | high | 1 | 1 |
| 4 | `WL-0MWXJGXSM009QA25` AC persistence, JSONL and sync | feature | high | 3 | 1 |
| 5 | `WL-0MWXJGZZB005JANC` wl ac CLI commands | feature | high | 4 | 1 |
| 6 | `WL-0MWXJH2DA007IGC2` wl show renders table criteria | feature | medium | 5 | 1 |
| 7 | `WL-0MWXJH4CC001V5G9` AC back-fill migration | feature | high | 1, 3, 4 | 1 |
| 8 | `WL-0MWXJH6GF004A7KF` Audit fingerprint schema 3 | feature | medium | 4, `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` | 2 |
| 9 | `WL-0MWXJHABR009PRVP` AC strip migration | feature | medium | 7, `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` | 2 |
| 10 | `WL-0MWXJHCVR0056VMB` AC docs and suite handoff | docs | medium | 8, 9 | 2 |
| 11 | `WL-0MWXJHG8M003F4BQ` Cross-repo AC blocker contract | task | medium | `WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` | 1 |

**Vertical-slice check.** Each child cuts through all layers it touches
(implementation, tests, docs, and — where relevant — sync/infra). No child is a
bare horizontal layer: the extractor (1) ships with its fixture corpus and parity
test; schema (3) ships with its cascade/CHECK tests; persistence (4) ships with
round-trip and delta-merge tests; the CLI (5) ships with exit-code tests; the two
migrations (7, 9) each ship with idempotence/dry-run tests; the fingerprint change
(8) ships with parity-set and sensitivity tests.

**Delivery sequence (matches the accepted Q1 = A + Q2 = C contract).**

1. **Landing 1 (children 1–7 and 11)** — table, CRUD/JSONL/sync, `wl ac` CLI,
   `wl show` rendering, the back-fill migration (descriptions untouched), docs.
   Every existing skill keeps parsing prose, so nothing breaks.
2. **`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`** (cross-repo) — skills read the table.
3. **Landing 2 (children 8–10)** — audit fingerprint schema 3 (in lockstep with
   the SorraAgents audit skill, accepted-schema set during the transition) and
   the strip migration, then this item reaches `in_review`.

Between landings: re-read children 8–10 and update their descriptions against
what actually shipped in landing 1 before starting them.

**Reuse identified.** The `startOn` slice `WL-0MWMGEPY2004EDZ8` is the template
for the paired version bump, migration entry and doctor check;
`packages/shared/src/database/comments.ts` + `mergeComments` are the templates for
AC CRUD and sync merging; `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts` already owns the
fail-on-skew probe that becomes a declared-schema set; the Python
`tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` is the parity oracle rather than
something to rewrite.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-26 — plan created: 11 children, 14 local dependency edges and 2
  cross-repo edges wired; effort Large / risk High confirmed above the planning
  threshold (approval gate not triggered: effort is not Extra Large).
- 2026-11-26 — Key Files corrected: `docs/CLI.md`, `docs/DATA_FORMAT.md` and
  `docs/DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` are at the repository root (`CLI.md`,
  `DATA_FORMAT.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`); `docs/migrations.md` added;
  `tests/migrations/*ac*` replaced with the real test locations
  (`tests/cli/ac-*.test.ts`, `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-*.test.ts`); the new
  `packages/shared/src/acceptance-criteria.ts` extractor added.
- 2026-11-26 — AC coverage review: all 15 parent acceptance criteria are covered
  by the children (`proceed`, no auto-closed gaps).

### Appendix additions (plan stage)

- Q8 (routine — settled by repo research): *Where do the docs named in the Key
  Files actually live?* — Answer (agent): `CLI.md`, `DATA_FORMAT.md` and
  `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` are at the repository root, not under `docs/`;
  migration policy is `docs/migrations.md` plus `docs/migrations/`. Source: `ls`
  of the repository root and `docs/`. Key Files corrected accordingly.
- Q9 (routine — settled by repo research): *Which id namespace do AC rows use?*
  — Answer (agent): `<prefix>-A<unique>` from the existing `generateUniqueId`
  helper, matching the comment convention `<prefix>-C<unique>`
  (`packages/shared/src/database/context.ts:538` `generateCommentId`), so AC ids
  cannot collide with work-item ids (`<prefix>-<unique>`) or comment ids.
- Q10 (routine — settled by repo research): *Does an AC write need a bespoke
  read-cache invalidation path?* — Answer (agent): no dedicated hook is needed —
  the CLI's `preAction` bumps the read-cache state counter for every command that
  is not a cacheable read (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`), so `wl ac add` invalidates
  by construction; the child asserts the behaviour rather than adding a new path.
- Q11 (routine — settled by repo research): *How does `wl ac search` query the
  criteria?* — Answer (agent): `LIKE` over `acceptance_criteria.text` ordered by
  owning item then `position`, with the existing search command as the JSON
  contract (`src/commands/search.ts`); a dedicated FTS table is not justified for
  ~15k short rows and would add a second index to keep in sync on every AC write.
  Recorded as an implementation choice, not a requirement change.
- Q12 (routine — settled by the accepted delivery sequence): *Do the fingerprint
  schema-3 bump and the strip migration ship in the same landing?* — Answer
  (agent): yes, both are landing 2 and both are blocked by
  `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`; they are separate child items so the strip can be held
  back independently if the re-audit wave needs scheduling. Source: parent
  "Risks and assumptions" delivery sequence (Q1 = A + Q2 = C).

# Evaluate moving ContextHub to Pi Durable

## Problem statement

ContextHub (Worklog) is a sizeable custom platform built from three layers — a
SQLite+JSONL issue tracker (`wl`), a Herdr orchestration/dispatch plugin, and a Pi
extension — maintained and evolved in-house. `@earendil-works/pi-durable` is a new
durable agent-harness platform (conversations, durable tasks, tools, hooks, signals,
subagents, custom documents, pluggable storage) that overlaps some of ContextHub's
orchestration and persistence concerns but not others. Before committing any
engineering effort to a port, the producer needs a single evidence-based overview
that maps ContextHub's features onto Pi Durable, flags the features that do **not**
map well, and states plainly whether a port makes sense.

## Users

- **Producer / technical decision-maker** — decides whether to fund a port, a partial
  re-platform, or neither. Wants a one-page verdict plus a feature-by-feature mapping.
- **Maintainer / implementing engineer** — needs to know which areas would be a
  rewrite, which would be a wrapper, and which have no home in Pi Durable, so effort
  can be estimated later.
- **AI agent operators** — indirectly affected; a port would change dispatch,
  durability, and recovery behaviour they rely on.

Example user stories:

- As the producer, I want an overview table mapping each ContextHub feature to how it
  would be re-implemented in Pi Durable, so that I can make a go/no-go decision.
- As a maintainer, I want the features that do not map well called out with reasons,
  so that I can see the true cost of a port before planning it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single evaluation document exists at `docs/dev/pi-durable-migration-evaluation.md` containing an overview table that enumerates **every** major ContextHub feature area (issue-tracker core; SQLite/JSONL persistence & migrations; Git-backed sync & multi-project/cross-repo; GitHub Issues mirroring; CLI + REST API + completion; plugin system; audit/review/claim lifecycle; Herdr worklist UI; agent dispatch/orchestration incl. downtime worker, hydrator, local-LLM idle dispatch; Pi extension modules; maintenance routines; interview/local-LLM; doctor/repair; AGENTS.md workflow integration) and describes, in 2–3 sentences per row, how that feature might be re-implemented in Pi Durable.
- The document explicitly **highlights** every feature that does not map well (or has no viable home) in Pi Durable, with a one-line rationale for each such flag.
- The document ends with a clear, reasoned **recommendation** (port / partial re-platform / do not port) tied to the mapping evidence, and names the top risks and unknowns of a port.
- The mapping table and recommendation are grounded in the Pi Durable README (the cited source of truth) and ContextHub's own README/docs, with claims traceable to a feature area rather than speculative.
- All content is written in UK English, and the document is linked from the repository's relevant documentation index where a "dev investigation" document would be discovered.
- All related documentation (README/docs references) is updated to reflect the new evaluation document.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A maintainer can read one document and understand, feature by feature, what porting ContextHub to Pi Durable would cost and where it would break, and the producer can make a go/no-go decision without commissioning a full migration spike.

## Constraints

- **Research/evaluation only — no port and no production code changes.** The deliverable is a decision document. Any implementation is out of scope and must be captured as separate follow-up work items if the recommendation is "port".
- Use the Pi Durable README (`https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/durable/README.md`) as the authoritative description of Pi Durable; note the README marks the package **experimental** (API changes without notice), which is itself a risk to record.
- Do not modify `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`, or other agent-infrastructure directories as part of this evaluation.
- Keep the document concise enough to be decision-useful (aim for an overview, not an exhaustive spec: 2–3 sentences per feature row).
- Follow the repository's existing investigation-doc conventions under `docs/dev/`.

## Existing state

ContextHub is a large, multi-package TypeScript monorepo:

- **Issue tracker core** (`src/`, `wl` CLI): work items with hierarchy, stages/status,
  priorities, types, tags, comments, dependencies, soft-delete, sort order, audit/review
  flags, claim/hold lifecycle.
- **Persistence**: SQLite as the runtime source of truth (`.worklog/worklog.db`) with an
  ephemeral JSONL pattern for Git transport, plus a migration system and doctor/repair
  tooling.
- **Sync**: `wl sync` (pull/merge/push JSONL), incremental/delta sync, author-identity
  gate, multi-project prefixes, cross-repo dependencies.
- **GitHub mirroring**: `wl github push/import` with label mapping, hierarchy, throttling.
- **Interfaces**: `wl` CLI (many subcommands), REST API (`src/api.ts`), shell completion.
- **Plugin system** for custom CLI commands.
- **Herdr plugin** (`packages/herdr/`): worklist UI — browse/filter/hierarchy/detail, chord
  shortcuts, metadata panel, markdown viewer, code-freeze awareness, plus agent dispatch,
  the downtime worker, hydrator (self-healing claims), local-LLM idle dispatch and local
  capacity reservation.
- **Pi extension** (`packages/tui/extensions/`): activity indicator, session-health footer,
  model/provider display, guardrails, `skill_path` tool, `/retry` error recovery, lease
  release, local preference.
- **Workflow assets**: maintenance-routines skill, `wl interview` local-LLM path,
  `AGENTS.md` workflow guidance and stage lifecycle.

## Desired change

Add `docs/dev/pi-durable-migration-evaluation.md` containing:

1. A short framing (what ContextHub is, what Pi Durable is, what "port" could mean).
2. The overview table: one row per major ContextHub feature area, each with a 2–3
   sentence description of a plausible Pi Durable re-implementation.
3. A clearly marked "Does not map well" section listing the flagged features and why.
4. A recommendation (port / partial re-platform / do not port) with top risks and
   unknowns (including Pi Durable's experimental status).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — all major features are in scope.** The table covers every major
  feature area rather than a chosen subset; a narrower read would understate the
  port's cost. If the producer wants a subset, this changes effort, not the AC shape.
- **Assumption — spike only, no code.** No port or production change is made; any
  port follows as separate work items. A wrong guess here is cheaply reversible
  because no code is touched.
- **Risk — Pi Durable is experimental.** Its README states the API "changes without
  notice between releases"; the evaluation must record this as a port risk, not just
  a caveat.
- **Risk — apples-to-oranges mapping.** Pi Durable is an agent runtime (conversations,
  durable tasks, tools, hooks); ContextHub is primarily an issue tracker plus an
  orchestration layer. The evaluation must distinguish "re-implementable on Pi Durable"
  from "belongs in a different layer" so the table does not imply false parity.
- **Scope-creep guard.** New opportunities surfaced during the evaluation (e.g. a
  proof-of-concept, a spun-out tool) must be recorded as linked follow-up work items,
  not folded into this item's scope.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/pi-durable-migration-evaluation.md` — New evaluation document: framing, overview table, non-mapping section, recommendation, risks.
- `README.md` — Link the new evaluation doc from the documentation index if a dev-investigation entry is expected there.
- `docs/dev/` — Follow existing `*-investigation.md` / evaluation doc conventions.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` and `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — Source material for the orchestration and extension feature rows.
- `API.md`, `CLI.md`, `DATA_SYNCING.md`, `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md` — Source material for the tracker, sync, and interface feature rows.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7** — Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless `pi -p` vs herdr pane (`send-to-pi.sh`). Adjacent dispatch decision; informs the "agent dispatch" row.
- **WL-0MP0E0M5500846SL** — Agent-centric Pi-based TUI for Worklog CLI. Prior Pi-based-interface attempt; relevant context for what Pi-adjacent surfaces ContextHub already explored (and later removed).
- **Pi Durable README** — `https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/durable/README.md` (captured as source `SRC-2026-11-26-006`).
- **WL-0MWXBZEYH001GFBX** — This work item.

Automated `find-related` scan (WL-0MWXBZEYH001GFBX) additionally surfaced the
following items/repo files via generic-keyword overlap; they are tangential and
recorded for traceability only:

- **WL-0MMBMCKN6024NXN6** — Migrate repository to git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/ContextHub (completed).
- **WL-0MWGO5IL3007JIFD** — Tests: push-authority gate decision matrix (completed).
- **WL-0MKRRZ2DN1M2289R** — `wl show` is not showing human readable output (completed).
- Repo files: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (matched on generic keywords such as "feature"/"readme").

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is the scope of 'ContextHub features' to evaluate — all of them or a subset?"
  Answer (agent, research): "All major feature areas." Research: README feature list plus
  package layout (`src/commands`, `packages/herdr`, `packages/tui/extensions`, `packages/shared`)
  enumerates the surface; the work item says "lists ContextHub features" without narrowing.
  Recorded as a documented assumption (routine — repo-answerable).
- Q: "Is this a research spike only, or does it include a proof-of-concept port?"
  Answer (agent, research): "Research/evaluation only." Research: the work item asks to
  "evaluate whether or not it makes sense to port" and to "create an overview table",
  which is a decision artifact, not a migration. Recorded as a documented assumption
  (routine — cheaply reversible; any port would be separate follow-up items).
- Q: "Where should the evaluation document live?"
  Answer (agent, research): "`docs/dev/pi-durable-migration-evaluation.md`." Research:
  `docs/dev/` already holds precedent investigation/evaluation documents (e.g.
  `chrome-headless-orchestrator-investigation.md`, `wal-checkpointing-investigation.md`).
  Recorded as a documented assumption (routine — repo-answerable).
- Q: "Must the document cite a recommendation, or only present the table?"
  Answer (agent, research): "Yes — a clear recommendation." Research: the work item title
  and body are framed as a go/no-go evaluation ("whether or not it makes sense to port"),
  so a verdict is part of the deliverable. Recorded as a documented assumption (routine).
- Duplicate check: searched `pi durable`, `durable`, `port`, `migration platform`,
  `evaluation` — no overlapping completed item; adjacent items linked under Related work.

# AC extraction parity harness (test-first)

## Goal

Land the TypeScript acceptance-criteria extractor **as a tested artefact before any
schema or migration work**, so the back-fill migration (F3, F4) is written against
a proven parser instead of an ad-hoc regex. As an implementing agent I want one
TypeScript function that returns exactly the criteria the Python skill parser
returns, so migrated rows and skill reads cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Characterisation tests cover the migration against a real-world fixture of the AC shapes actually present in the worklog (checkbox `- [ ]`, bold-led, period- and paren-numbered, hard-wrapped multi-line, nested sub-bullets), and prove extraction parity with `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` for the same text.
- A TypeScript `extractAcceptanceCriteria(description)` helper in a new `packages/shared/src/acceptance-criteria.ts` returns the ordered criterion list for a description, matching the Python marker rules: `- `, `+ `, `1. ` and `1)` in document order, markers indented deeper than the first AC marker treated as nested detail (not criteria), hard-wrapped continuation lines joined, `*` star bullets NOT recognised.
- Fixtures live under `tests/fixtures/acceptance-criteria/` and are derived read-only from this store's real descriptions (the shapes counted in the parent's "Existing state" table), each recording the description excerpt and the expected ordered criteria.
- The parity test compares TypeScript output with the Python helper field-for-field (text, order) over every fixture, fails on any disagreement, and skips only with an explicit recorded reason when `python3` or the skills helper is unavailable.
- Tests for the five measured shape families (checkbox `- [ ]`, bold-led, numbered, wrapped, nested) each assert the exact expected list, so a regression names the failing shape family.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `acceptance-criteria.ts` to `packages/shared/src` and export it from the package index.
- Copy 10–15 representative descriptions out of `.worklog/worklog.db` into JSON fixtures (no secrets; descriptions only).
- Add `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-extraction.test.ts` (shape families) and `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-parity.test.ts` (Python cross-check, subprocess probe guarded like `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts`).

## Dependencies

- None. This is the first item of the delivery sequence.

## Deliverables

- `packages/shared/src/acceptance-criteria.ts` — the extractor.
- `tests/fixtures/acceptance-criteria/*.json` — the fixture corpus.
- Two passing test files (shape families + Python parity).

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/acceptance-criteria.ts` — **new** extractor module.
- `tests/fixtures/acceptance-criteria/` — **new** fixture corpus.
- `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-extraction.test.ts`, `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-parity.test.ts` — **new** tests.
- `../SorraAgents/skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — reference implementation for parity (`extract_acceptance_criteria`).

## Notes

- The structural precedent is `WL-0MVO93BBC000H734` (numbered-list marker rules).
- No schema change here — this slice is deliberately test-first and unblocks F3/F4.

# AC status advisory guard (test)

## Goal

Prove, by test, that moving acceptance criteria into a table does **not** quietly
introduce a gate. Producer decision Q3 = A: status is stored, rendered and
queryable only. As an operator I want a regression test that fails the moment
someone makes `wl next`, `worklist`, `audit` or `doctor` branch on AC status.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC status is **advisory** in this delivery (producer decision Q3 = A): no gate — `wl next`, `worklist`, `audit`, `doctor`, or any skill — may block, warn or otherwise branch on AC status; statuses are stored, rendered and queryable only.
- An automated test asserts that `wl next`, `wl worklist --json`, `wl audit` and `wl doctor` produce byte-identical output for an item whose criteria are all `met` and for the same item with every criterion `unmet` (status is invisible to selection and gating).
- A source-level guard test asserts no module outside the AC data layer and the display/query commands references the status column in a selection, gating or warning path (`rg`-style assertion over `src/` excluding `src/commands/ac.ts`, `src/commands/show.ts` and `packages/shared/src/database/`).
- The advisory rule is stated in `docs/dev/acceptance-criteria.md` and cross-referenced from the `wl ac` section of `CLI.md`.

## Minimal implementation

- Create an item with three criteria, run the four gate commands, snapshot the JSON, flip statuses, re-run, compare.
- Add the source-level assertion as a small test that greps for `acceptance_criteria.status` / `.status` misuse in gate modules.
- Document the rule (one paragraph + link to the producer decision in the parent).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `wl ac` CLI (`WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` child "wl ac CLI commands" (`WL-0MWXJGZZB005JANC`)) — needs a way to set status.

## Deliverables

- Documented advisory rule.

## Key Files

- `src/next.ts`, `src/commands/worklist.ts`, `src/audit.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts` — read-only subjects of the guard.
- `docs/dev/acceptance-criteria.md` — **new**.

# acceptance_criteria schema and version bump

## Goal

Give acceptance criteria first-class storage: a new `acceptance_criteria` table
with its own stable id, owning work item, text, status, stated order and the
"modified" provenance fields. As an agent I want to read ACs as rows so I never
regex a description again; as a reviewer I want a modified criterion to keep the
original wording and the justification for the change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `acceptance_criteria` table exists in the SQLite schema with, at least, an AC id, the owning work item id (FK to `workitems(id)`, `ON DELETE CASCADE`), the criterion text, a status constrained to `met|unmet|partial|modified`, a stable ordering column, and — for `modified` rows — the original criterion text and the justification for the change; `SCHEMA_VERSION` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`) and `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`src/migrations/index.ts`) are bumped together by exactly one step (10 → 11).
- `acceptance_criteria` is added to `REQUIRED_TABLES` and to the additive-column/table self-heal path, so a fresh `wl init` creates it and a store written by an older release gains it on `wl doctor upgrade`.
- An AC row is removed when its owning work item is deleted (`ON DELETE CASCADE` proven by a test), the status CHECK constraint rejects any value outside `met|unmet|partial|modified`, and `position` is a non-null integer with a unique `(work_item_id, position)` index.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` exports `AcceptanceCriterion` and an `AcceptanceCriterionStatus` union, used by the database, JSONL and CLI layers so the status vocabulary is declared once.
- A schema test asserts the table shape, the FK cascade, the status CHECK and the paired version constants, and `wl doctor` reports no schema mismatch on a store it has just created.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the DDL + indexes in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` next to the `audit_results` table, add the `REQUIRED_TABLES` entry, bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` to 11.
- Add a `__table:acceptance_criteria` entry to the migration catalog and bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` to `'11'`.
- Add the types; add `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-schema.test.ts`.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "AC extraction parity harness" (`WL-0MWXJGRML004YI6O`) (test-first ordering: the parser lands before the storage that will be filled from it).
- Template: `WL-0MWMGEPY2004EDZ8` (`startOn`) for the paired version bump + doctor check shape.

## Deliverables

- Table DDL, indexes, `REQUIRED_TABLES` entry, paired version bump.
- `AcceptanceCriterion` / status union types.
- Schema + cascade + CHECK tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — DDL, indexes, `REQUIRED_TABLES`, `SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — catalog entry, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — `AcceptanceCriterion`, `AcceptanceCriterionStatus`.
- `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-schema.test.ts` — **new**.

## Notes

- Additive migration only; no destructive rewrite of `workitems` (see `docs/migrations.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`).
- No description rewriting happens in this item — that is the strip migration, a later separately-runnable step (Q1 = A).

# AC persistence, JSONL and sync

## Goal

Make AC rows durable and shareable: CRUD on the shared database layer, a
`acceptance_criterion` JSONL record type, and delta-merge support in Git sync, so
two stores converge on the same criteria without dropping each other's rows. As
an agent I want my criteria edits to travel with `wl sync` like comments do.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC rows round-trip through JSONL export/import and Git sync as their own record type: a full export → import into an empty store reproduces every row exactly (text, status, ordering, original + justification), and a delta sync between an ahead and a behind store carries AC additions, updates and deletions without dropping the behind store's other rows.
- `packages/shared/src/database/` exposes AC CRUD (`addAcceptanceCriterion`, `getAcceptanceCriteria`, `updateAcceptanceCriterion`, `deleteAcceptanceCriterion`, `searchAcceptanceCriteria`) mirroring the existing comment methods, with `getAcceptanceCriteria(workItemId)` returning `position` order.
- AC ids are generated as `<prefix>-A<unique>` through the existing `generateUniqueId` helper, so they never collide with work-item (`<prefix>-<unique>`) or comment (`<prefix>-C<unique>`) ids; a test asserts the namespace and its uniqueness.
- `src/jsonl.ts` emits and parses `{type: 'acceptance_criterion'}` records in a deterministic order (owning item, then position) and old parsers that only know `workitem`/`comment`/`audit_result` skip the new type without error.
- A delta sync merges AC rows through `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts` (a `mergeAcceptanceCriteria` peer of `mergeComments`) at both sync call sites, and a deleted criterion is not resurrected by an older peer.
- Every AC write bumps the read-cache state counter, so `wl show --json` immediately after `wl ac add` returns the new criterion list (no stale cache entry).
- Changed-scope tests cover JSONL round-trip (full export → import into an empty store, field-identical rows).

## Minimal implementation

- CRUD module beside `packages/shared/src/database/comments.ts`; `generateAcceptanceCriterionId` peer of `generateCommentId`.
- Extend `src/jsonl.ts` export/import (both the sync and worker export paths).
- Add `mergeAcceptanceCriteria` to `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts`; wire it in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/sync/remote.ts` (replay chain) and `src/commands/migrate.ts`.
- Tests: round-trip, delta merge (add/update/delete), id namespace, cache invalidation.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "acceptance_criteria schema and version bump" (`WL-0MWXJGVOQ0068QWK`) (needs the table and types).
- Read-cache behaviour reference: `src/read-cache-cli.ts` (`invalidateCacheForWrite`).

## Deliverables

- Database CRUD + id generation.
- JSONL record type in export and import.
- Sync merge + call-site wiring.
- Round-trip, delta-merge, id-namespace and cache-invalidation tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (+ `packages/shared/src/database/`) — AC CRUD and id generation.
- `src/jsonl.ts` — `acceptance_criterion` record type, export and import.
- `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts`, `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/sync/remote.ts`, `src/commands/migrate.ts` — merge wiring.
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — write-invalidation path.
- `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-jsonl.test.ts`, `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-merge.test.ts` — **new**.

## Notes

- The prefix filter (`src/sync/prefix-filter.ts`) and the foreign-edge bug `WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` are out of scope here; AC rows belong to own-prefix items, so they are filtered exactly like comments.

# wl ac CLI commands

## Goal

Give every consumer a first-class way to work with criteria from the shell: add,
delete, update, show and search. As an implementing agent I want
`wl ac show <id> --json` to hand me ordered rows with status instead of parsing
prose; as an operator I want `wl ac search "<text>"` to return the matching
criteria with their owning items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl ac add`, `wl ac delete`, `wl ac update`, `wl ac show` and `wl ac search` exist and behave per this contract: `show <work-item-id>` lists that item's criteria in document order with their status; `search <text>` returns matching criteria **and** their owning work item id + title; all five support `--json` and non-zero exit codes for unknown ids and invalid arguments.
- `wl ac update --status modified` requires the original criterion text and the justification (rejects the invocation with a non-zero exit and an explanatory message when either is missing), and stores both on the row.
- `wl ac add` appends at the next free `position` by default and accepts an explicit `--position` to insert or reorder without renumbering the remaining rows.
- `wl ac` is registered in `src/command-registry.ts`, appears in grouped `wl --help` output and in shell completion, and loads through the `COMMAND_LOADERS` heavy graph so the `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` budget is unaffected.
- `wl ac search` reuses the existing search plumbing (`worklog_fts` where it covers the table, otherwise an equivalent `LIKE` fallback with the same ordering semantics), returning owning-item id + title with each hit.
- Changed-scope tests cover CLI CRUD + exit codes.

## Minimal implementation

- New `src/commands/ac.ts` with an `ac` subcommand group, following `src/commands/comment.ts` for shape and `src/commands/cli-utils.ts` for JSON/exit-code helpers.
- Register in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES` and `COMMAND_LOADERS` (`src/command-registry.ts`); verify grouped help and completion output.
- Tests: `tests/cli/ac-add.test.ts`, `ac-update.test.ts`, `ac-delete.test.ts`, `ac-show.test.ts`, `ac-search.test.ts` (JSON + human forms, exit codes, invalid args, registration/help/completion assertions).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "AC persistence, JSONL and sync" (`WL-0MWXJGXSM009QA25`) (needs CRUD on the shared database layer).

## Deliverables

- `src/commands/ac.ts` with five subcommands.
- Registry + help + completion entries.
- CLI tests covering CRUD, JSON output and exit codes.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/ac.ts` — **new**.
- `src/command-registry.ts` — `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES`, `COMMAND_LOADERS`.
- `src/commands/cli-utils.ts`, `src/commands/comment.ts` — shape/helpers to mirror.
- `tests/cli/ac-*.test.ts` — **new**.

## Notes

- AC status is advisory (Q3 = A); the CLI must not warn or gate on it.
- `--json` output shape: `{ success, criteria: [{ id, workItemId, position, text, status, originalText, modificationJustification }] }`; `search` adds `workItemTitle`.

# wl show renders table criteria

## Goal

Make `wl show` the single call an agent needs: the item's criteria come back from
the table, in order, with status (and modification provenance). No second query,
no prose parsing. As a reviewer I want to see at a glance which criteria are met,
unmet, partial or modified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl show <id>` renders the item's criteria from the table so a consumer needs no second query.
- The rendered block is ordered by `position`, shows each criterion's status, and for `modified` rows prints the original wording plus the justification for the change.
- `wl show <id> --json` exposes the same criteria as structured rows (`acceptanceCriteria: [...]`), so a JSON consumer reads one document.
- While an item's own `## Acceptance Criteria` description section still exists (unmigrated store or after the back-fill landing but before the strip), `wl show` renders the table rows when the item has any and falls back to the description block otherwise, so no item loses its criteria mid-sequence; the fallback is removed by the strip migration.
- Changed-scope tests cover the rendered block, the JSON field and the fallback path.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `src/commands/show.ts` to read the item's rows from the database and render a dedicated section; include the rows in the `--json` payload.
- Keep the existing description rendering untouched apart from not duplicating the AC block when table rows exist.

# AC back-fill migration

## Goal

Populate the new table from the ~3,020 descriptions that already carry an
`## Acceptance Criteria` section, **without touching the descriptions**, so
exactly one landing is needed before the SorraAgents skills switch
(`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`) and every existing skill keeps working in the interim
(delivery sequence step 1, Q1 = A + Q2 = C).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A migration under `src/migrations/index.ts` iterates every **non-deleted** work item that has an `## Acceptance Criteria` section, inserts one row per criterion in document order, and is idempotent — re-running creates no duplicate rows, and deleted work items yield zero rows.
- Both migrations report a summary (items scanned, criteria inserted, descriptions stripped, items skipped/unparseable) and `--dry-run` prints the same counts without writing; both are classified `safe: true` and run inside the existing single transaction.
- Migrated criteria default to status `unmet` (checkbox state is not a status signal: 61 ticked of 3,103) and take `position` from document order starting at 0.
- The back-fill performs **no description change** — every description keeps its `## Acceptance Criteria` section in this landing, so the current description-based parse in the skills keeps working unchanged (compatibility contract, AC "Cross-repo and compatibility").
- A section that parses to zero criteria inserts no rows, is counted as `skipped/unparseable` in the summary, and its id is listed so the gap is visible rather than silently dropped.
- The migration is proven idempotent with a test that runs it twice on a copy of a real-world fixture and asserts row-for-row equality, and its run time on a copy of this store (~15,172 criteria / ~3,020 descriptions) is measured and recorded in this work item.

## Minimal implementation

# Audit fingerprint schema 3

## Goal

Keep audit freshness honest once criteria live in the table: an AC edit must
invalidate a stored audit exactly as a description edit does today. As a
reviewer I want a re-worded criterion to make the audit stale, and I want the
one-off re-audit wave visible in `wl doctor` instead of silently absorbed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The audit content fingerprint moves to **schema 3** over `title` + `description` + the item's **ordered AC rows** (id, position, text, status), so an edit to a criterion invalidates a stored audit exactly as a description edit does today; schema-2 digests are treated as stale, and the bounded re-audit wave (358 stored fingerprints on this store, mostly old completed items) is surfaced by `wl doctor` rather than silently absorbed.
- The fingerprint schema bump ships **in lockstep** with `../SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA`, `_compute_content_fingerprint`): the parity check is fail-on-skew (`src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts`, `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts`), so a one-sided bump turns `dev` red and a one-sided digest makes every audit read stale. The transition must accept a declared-schema **set** (the union of the old and new version) on both sides until both repositories have shipped.
- `computeContentFingerprint` accepts the item's ordered AC rows and includes them in the canonical payload; both call sites (`src/list-enrichment.ts`, `src/commands/update.ts`) pass the rows, so `wl list` freshness and `wl update` re-fingerprinting agree.
- The installed-side probe validates the declared schema against an accepted **set** `{2, 3}` during the transition (not a single literal), and the parity test covers a schema-2 peer, a schema-3 peer and an out-of-set peer (the last must fail).
- `wl doctor` reports the stale-fingerprint wave with counts and the affected work-item id list before the strip migration runs, so the re-audit cost is scheduled rather than discovered.
- Changed-scope tests cover the digest change: editing only a criterion's text or status changes the digest, and no other item's digest moves.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the payload in `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` (schema 3) and thread `acceptanceCriteria` through both call sites.
- Relax `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts` to an accepted-schema set; extend `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts`.
- Add the doctor report (a doctor notice/subcommand beside the existing audit-gap checks) listing stale-by-schema rows.
- Tests: digest sensitivity, doctor report contents, parity set acceptance.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "AC persistence, JSONL and sync" (`WL-0MWXJGXSM009QA25`) (the rows must exist and be readable).
- Blocked by **`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`** (cross-repo): per the accepted delivery sequence this ships in landing 2, in lockstep with the SorraAgents audit skill.
- Documentation contract: `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md`.

## Deliverables

- Schema-3 fingerprint over ordered AC rows.
- Declared-schema-set acceptance in the installed probe + parity tests.
- `wl doctor` stale-wave report.
- Digest-sensitivity tests.

## Key Files

- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA`, `computeContentFingerprint`.
- `src/audit-fingerprint-installed.ts` — accepted-schema set.
- `src/list-enrichment.ts`, `src/commands/update.ts` — call sites.
- `src/commands/doctor/` — stale-wave report.
- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit-fingerprint-schema3.test.ts` — parity + sensitivity.
- `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` — contract update.

## Notes

- The one-sided bump failure mode is known (`dev` red on parity skew); the accepted-schema set is the mitigation and must land in the same change as the TS bump.
- The SorraAgents half of the lockstep belongs to the cross-repo item; do not edit `../SorraAgents` from this worktree.

# AC strip migration

## Goal

Finish the move to a single source of truth: once the skills read the table
(`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` landed), remove the `## Acceptance Criteria` section from
every migrated description. As an operator I want the second landing to be
separately runnable and resumable, so a partially applied run never leaves a
description half-stripped or a criterion lost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The back-fill and the strip are **two separately-runnable migrations**, not one atomic step, so the strip can be sequenced after `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` lands: the second migration removes the `## Acceptance Criteria` section from every migrated description (the table becomes the sole source of truth — producer decision Q1 = A), is idempotent and re-runnable, leaves every other description section untouched, and records each stripped item so a partially applied run can be resumed.
- Both migrations report a summary (items scanned, criteria inserted, descriptions stripped, items skipped/unparseable) and `--dry-run` prints the same counts without writing; both are classified `safe: true` and run inside the existing single transaction.
- The strip refuses to remove a section for an item that has zero AC rows (records it as `skipped: no rows` instead), so prose can never be dropped without a table copy.
- Recorded stripped ids live in metadata (`acceptanceCriteriaStripped`), are written per item as the run proceeds, and a resumed run skips them; a test interrupts after N items and asserts the resumed run strips exactly the remainder.
- Only the `## Acceptance Criteria` heading and its list body are removed: every other `##` section, the title line and trailing content are byte-identical before and after, proven by a fixture test.

## Minimal implementation

- Second migration entry (e.g. `__meta:acceptanceCriteriaStripped`) that rewrites `workitems.description` for items with rows and an AC section; counts + dry-run through the same logger contract as the back-fill.
- Write the stripped-id record as it goes; resume by reading it back.
- Tests: `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-strip-migration.test.ts` (idempotence, resumability, section surgery, dry-run, zero-row refusal).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "AC back-fill migration" (`WL-0MWXJH4CC001V5G9`) (rows must exist first).
- Blocked by **`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`** (cross-repo): the skills must read the table before the prose disappears. This is delivery sequence step 3 — do not start before that item completes.

## Deliverables

- Strip migration entry with resumable progress recording, summary and dry-run.
- Idempotence, resumability and section-surgery tests.

## Key Files

- `src/migrations/index.ts` — strip migration entry + metadata marker.
- `tests/unit/acceptance-criteria-strip-migration.test.ts` — **new**.
- `docs/migrations.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — migration documentation.

## Notes

- Runs inside the existing single transaction (so "resume" means *re-run after a failure*, using the recorded ids rather than a long-lived transaction).
- This is the change that invalidates the 358 stored audit fingerprints' inputs; it ships with "Audit fingerprint schema 3" (`WL-0MWXJH6GF004A7KF`).

# Cross-repo AC blocker contract

## Goal

Keep the Q2 = C sequencing guarantee enforceable and auditable: the cross-repo
blocker edge must survive `wl sync` once the prefix-filter bug is fixed, and the
compatibility contract that lets the skills keep parsing prose until
`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` lands must be written down in this repository, not only in
the intake Appendix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The cross-repo item is the recorded blocker: **`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`** (*Use the worklog acceptance-criteria table instead of parsing AC prose*, `high`, `open`, `../SorraAgents`) switches the skills that parse AC prose (at least `find-related` and `implement`, plus the shared `tree_coverage.py` extraction) onto the table, and the dependency edge `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` is recorded in this store, so this item cannot reach `in_review` until that item completes (producer decision Q2 = C). This item documents the compatibility contract that keeps the current description-based parse working until that item lands.
- A verification step asserts the edge is present via `wl dep list WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG --json` immediately before this item is marked `in_review`, and after `WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` (foreign edges dropped by the sync prefix filter) is completed the edge is asserted to survive a full `wl sync` cycle.
- `docs/dev/acceptance-criteria.md` records the three-step delivery sequence, the interim compatibility rule (prose stays the fallback; `wl show` falls back to it), and the statement that the blocker is repeated in prose in the parent description so it survives a dropped edge.
- The SorraAgents item is commented with the second-landing requirement it inherits: the fingerprint schema-3 lockstep (`_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` and `_compute_content_fingerprint`) and the accepted-schema-set transition window.
- No file in `../SorraAgents` is edited from this worktree; the only cross-repo action is a comment on the existing item through its own worklog store.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the contract section to `docs/dev/acceptance-criteria.md` (shared with "AC docs and suite handoff" (`WL-0MWXJHCVR0056VMB`)) and the three-step sequence to `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`.
- Add a small pre-`in_review` check script/snippet that verifies the edge (documented in the item comment, not a new CLI command).
- Comment the fingerprint lockstep requirement on `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` (critical: cross-repo edges dropped by the sync prefix filter) for the "survives sync" assertion.
- Related cross-repo item: `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`.

## Deliverables

- Documented compatibility contract and delivery sequence.
- Edge-presence verification recorded before `in_review`.
- Lockstep requirement commented on the SorraAgents item.

- `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — delivery-sequence note.
- `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — read-only reference for the dropped-edge bug.
